units.summary: Native American society before European Contact, European exploration in the New World, Exploration in the new World

events.title: Native American societies before contact
events.description: diverse societies adapted to their environments; maize cultivation spread north from Mexico, supporting settled societies like the Pueblo (irrigation, adobe homes) and the Mississippian mound builders (Cahokia); Great Plains and Great Basin peoples were mostly mobile hunter-gatherers; Northeast peoples like the Iroquois mixed farming (the 'Three Sisters': maize, beans, squash) with hunting in permanent villages; Pacific Northwest peoples relied on fishing and trade

events.title: Portuguese exploration of Africa
events.description: sponsored by Prince Henry the Navigator, Portuguese sailors explored the West African coast, set up trading posts, and began the Atlantic slave trade; used new technology like the caravel, compass, and astrolabe; Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope (1488) and Vasco da Gama reached India (1498)

events.title: Reconquista completed
events.description: Spain captured Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Spain; Spain was unified under Ferdinand and Isabella, who now had the resources and religious zeal to sponsor exploration

events.title: Columbus arrives in the New World
events.description: Sparks flow of trade between old and new world. Stimulates food production and growth. Spain becomes colonial power in the Americas

events.title: Columbian Exchange
events.description: transfer of plants, animals, and diseases between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres; Europe received maize, potatoes, and tomatoes, which fueled population growth; the Americas received horses, cattle, pigs, wheat, and sugar; smallpox and other diseases killed a large majority of Native Americans; American gold and silver fueled European economies and the shift toward capitalism

events.title: Treaty of Tordesillas
events.description: divided newly discovered lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal along a line west of the Cape Verde Islands; Spain received most of the Americas, while Portugal received Brazil and its routes to Africa and Asia

events.title: John Cabot reaches North America
events.description: sailed for England and reached Newfoundland, giving England a claim to North America

events.title: Encomienda system
events.description: Spanish colonial labor system in which the crown granted colonists the right to demand labor and tribute from Native Americans in exchange for converting them to Christianity; led to brutal treatment and population decline; gradually replaced by the hacienda system and African slavery

events.title: Casta system
events.description: Spanish racial hierarchy: peninsulares (born in Spain) at the top, then criollos (Spanish descent born in the Americas), mestizos (Spanish and Native), mulattoes (Spanish and African), and Native Americans and Africans at the bottom; reflected intermarriage in colonies with few Spanish women

events.title: Protestant Reformation
events.description: Martin Luther challenged the Catholic Church, splitting Christianity in Europe; rivalry between Catholic Spain and France and Protestant England and the Dutch shaped colonization and later drove religious dissenters to settle in North America

events.title: Cortés conquers the Aztecs
events.description: Hernán Cortés, aided by Native allies who resented Aztec rule and by a smallpox epidemic, captured Tenochtitlan in 1521; Spain gained massive wealth and built Mexico City on its ruins

events.title: Pizarro conquers the Inca
events.description: Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa and conquered the Inca Empire in Peru; silver from Andean mines like Potosí made Spain the wealthiest nation in Europe

events.title: Valladolid Debate
events.description: Bartolomé de las Casas argued Native Americans were fully human and should be treated fairly, while Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda argued they were 'natural slaves'; reflected European debates over how to treat Native Americans; Las Casas's earlier advocacy had helped produce the New Laws of 1542 limiting the encomienda

events.title: St. Augustine founded
events.description: founded by Spain in Florida; oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental U.S.

events.title: Roanoke Colony
events.description: England's first attempts at settlement in North America, sponsored by Sir Walter Raleigh; the colonists had vanished by 1590, becoming known as the 'Lost Colony'

events.title: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
events.description: the English navy defeated the Spanish Armada, weakening Spain's naval dominance and opening the way for English colonization of North America

events.title: Spanish colonize New Mexico
events.description: Juan de Oñate led Spanish settlement among the Pueblo peoples and brutally crushed resistance at Acoma Pueblo (1599); Spanish missionaries tried to convert the Pueblos to Catholicism, building resentment that led to the Pueblo Revolt

units.summary: Colonies established in the New World by the Spanish, French, Dutch, and British

events.title: Jamestown founded
events.description: first permanent English settlement in North America, founded by the joint-stock Virginia Company in search of profit; nearly collapsed from disease, conflict with the Powhatan Confederacy, and the 'Starving Time' (1609-1610); John Smith's 'no work, no food' rule helped it survive

events.title: Quebec founded
events.description: Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec; French colonists were few and focused on the fur trade, often intermarrying and allying with Native Americans such as the Huron

events.title: Tobacco cultivation in Virginia
events.description: John Rolfe introduced a sweeter strain of tobacco, creating a profitable cash crop; drove demand for land and labor, first met by indentured servants and later by enslaved Africans

events.title: Headright System
events.description: Virginia granted 50 acres of land to anyone who paid for a settler's passage, encouraging the importation of indentured servants

events.title: House of Burgesses
events.description: first representative legislative assembly in the English colonies, established in Virginia; beginning of colonial self-government

events.title: First Africans arrive in Virginia
events.description: about 20 enslaved Africans arrived at Point Comfort; their status was at first unclear, but over the 1600s colonial laws made slavery hereditary, lifelong, and based on race

events.title: Mayflower Compact and Plymouth Colony
events.description: Separatist Pilgrims signed the Mayflower Compact, an early agreement for self-government, before founding Plymouth; survived with help from Squanto and the Wampanoag

events.title: New Netherland founded
events.description: Dutch West India Company founded New Netherland, with New Amsterdam on Manhattan (1626), as a fur trading colony; religiously tolerant and diverse; taken by England in 1664 and renamed New York

events.title: Massachusetts Bay Colony
events.description: Puritans led by John Winthrop sought to build a model Christian community, a 'city upon a hill'; Great Migration of Puritan families in the 1630s; towns governed by town meetings, and only church members could vote

events.title: Maryland founded
events.description: proprietary colony founded by Lord Baltimore (Calvert family) as a refuge for Catholics; Maryland Toleration Act (1649) granted religious freedom to all Christians

events.title: Rhode Island founded
events.description: Roger Williams, banished from Massachusetts, founded Providence with separation of church and state and religious freedom; Anne Hutchinson, also banished for challenging Puritan ministers, settled there as well

events.title: Mercantilism
events.description: economic theory that a nation's wealth depends on a favorable balance of trade and accumulating gold and silver; colonies existed to supply raw materials to the mother country and buy its manufactured goods

events.title: Navigation Acts
events.description: series of English laws enforcing mercantilism: colonial trade had to be carried on English ships, and 'enumerated' goods like tobacco and sugar could be shipped only to England; widely evaded through smuggling

events.title: Carolina colony founded
events.description: settled largely by planters from Barbados, who brought the West Indian plantation system and slave codes; rice cultivation relied on enslaved Africans, making South Carolina a black-majority colony by the early 1700s

events.title: Metacom's War (King Philip's War)
events.description: Wampanoag leader Metacom led a Native alliance against New England colonists' expansion onto their land; devastating for both sides and ended Native resistance in southern New England

events.title: Bacon's Rebellion
events.description: Nathaniel Bacon led frontier farmers and former indentured servants against Governor Berkeley over his refusal to attack Native Americans and lack of available land; burned Jamestown; convinced planters to shift from indentured servants to enslaved Africans

events.title: Pueblo Revolt
events.description: Popé led the Pueblo peoples against Spanish rule and forced conversion in New Mexico, driving the Spanish out for twelve years; the Spanish returned in 1692 and showed more tolerance of Pueblo culture and religion

events.title: Pennsylvania founded
events.description: William Penn founded Pennsylvania as a Quaker colony with religious tolerance, a representative assembly, and fair dealings with the Lenape

events.title: Dominion of New England
events.description: James II combined the New England colonies (later New York and New Jersey) under Governor Edmund Andros and abolished their assemblies; colonists overthrew Andros after the Glorious Revolution

events.title: Glorious Revolution
events.description: Parliament replaced James II with William and Mary; the English Bill of Rights (1689) limited the monarchy; reinforced colonists' belief in the rights of Englishmen and representative government

events.title: Salem Witch Trials
events.description: mass hysteria in Salem, Massachusetts, led to the execution of 20 accused witches; reflected social tensions, economic rivalries, and Puritan anxieties

events.title: Salutary Neglect
events.description: unofficial British policy (especially under Prime Minister Robert Walpole) of loosely enforcing the Navigation Acts, allowing colonies to govern themselves and grow economically; ended after the French and Indian War

events.title: Triangular Trade and the Middle Passage
events.description: Atlantic trade network: manufactured goods to Africa, enslaved Africans to the Americas, and sugar, molasses, and tobacco to Europe and New England; millions of Africans endured the deadly Middle Passage across the Atlantic

events.title: Enlightenment
events.description: emphasized reason, science, and natural rights; John Locke argued people had rights to life, liberty, and property and that government rested on a social contract; spread through colonial print culture (Benjamin Franklin) and shaped later revolutionary ideas

events.title: Georgia founded
events.description: last of the thirteen colonies, founded by James Oglethorpe as a buffer against Spanish Florida and a haven for debtors; originally banned slavery, but the ban was lifted in 1751

events.title: First Great Awakening
events.description: Protestant revival led by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield; emphasized personal, emotional faith over church authority; split congregations (New Lights vs. Old Lights), founded colleges, and encouraged colonists to question authority

events.title: Zenger Trial
events.description: printer John Peter Zenger was acquitted of libel for criticizing New York's governor because what he printed was true; early step toward freedom of the press

events.title: Stono Rebellion
events.description: largest slave revolt in the British colonies, in South Carolina; rebels marched toward Spanish Florida, which promised freedom; led to harsher slave codes (Negro Act of 1740)

events.title: Albany Plan of Union
events.description: Benjamin Franklin proposed uniting the colonies under one council for defense and Native American relations at the start of the French and Indian War; rejected by the colonies and Britain but set a precedent for colonial unity ('Join, or Die' cartoon)

units.summary: American Revolution, the events that led up to it, and the formation of the United States

presidents.name: George Washington
presidents.description: First President of the United States

presidents.name: John Adams
presidents.description: Foreign Affairs with France

events.title: Seven Years' War/French and Indian War
events.description: global conflict between France and Great Britain; caused Britain to go double debt and increase taxes on colonists

events.title: Taxation without Representation
events.description: Colonial people didn't want the taxation without representation; British claims virtual representation that they represented everyone

events.title: Sugar Act
events.description: lowered the duty on molasses set by the Molasses Act of 1733 but strictly enforced it; first British tax meant to raise revenue from the colonies rather than just regulate trade

events.title: Currency Act
events.description: prohibited American colonies from issuing their own currency

events.title: Quartering Act
events.description: British law that required American colonies to provide housing and provisions to British soldiers

events.title: Stamp Act
events.description: after the Sugar Act, parliament taxed all printed papers such as legal documents, newspapers, and playing cards; repealed in 1766 after colonial boycotts hurt British merchants and many commended the colonists for resisting a tax passed when not represented

events.title: Declaratory Act
events.description: repeal of the Stamp Act made Parliament pass an act on the same day that stated Parliament could make laws binding the American colonies 'in all cases whatsoever'

events.title: Townshend Acts
events.description: taxes on imported glass, lead, paint, paper, and tea, with revenue used to pay royal governors and judges (taking away colonial assemblies' power over their salaries); led to colonial boycotts (non-importation agreements), John Dickinson's 'Letters from a Farmer in Pennsylvania,' and British troops stationed in Boston; all duties except the tax on tea were repealed in 1770

events.title: Boston Tea Party
events.description: American political and mercantile protest against tax on tea and 'taxation without representation'

events.title: Coercive Acts
events.description: called the 'Intolerable Acts' by colonists; punished Massachusetts for the Boston Tea Party by closing Boston Harbor until the tea was paid for, restricting town meetings and self-government, allowing royal officials to be tried in Britain, and expanding quartering of troops; led to the First Continental Congress

events.title: Thomas Paine's Common Sense
events.description: pamphlet written by Thomas Paine advocating for independence from Great Britain in the colonies; based heavily on enlightenment ideals

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.description: Articulated the principle of individual liberty and government's responsibility to serve the people; government gets its power from the consent of the governed and must protect natural rights (life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness)

events.title: American Revolutionary War
events.description: despite Britain's military and financial advantages, the American Patriots won the Revolutionary War and gained independence

events.title: Articles of Confederation
events.description: the first constitution of the United States of America, failed due to weak federal government; all government power in legislative, but weak, as many wanted weak government contrasting from strong British power

events.title: Shays' Rebellion
events.description: rebellion over debt; displayed weakness of government and inability to have army for domestic and international purposes

events.title: Constitutional Convention
events.description: to help rectify the weakness of the Articles of Confederation; the Great Compromise (Connecticut Compromise): Bicameral legislation; 3/5s Compromise: 3/5s of slave population counted towards population

events.title: Federalism
events.description: sharing of power between state and government;

events.title: Judiciary Act of 1789
events.description: Established courts below the Supreme Court

events.title: French Revolution
events.description: Social and political upheaval in France that divided American politics: Democratic-Republicans sympathized with France while Federalists favored Britain; led to Washington's Neutrality Proclamation (1793)

events.title: Bill of Rights is ratified
events.description: First ten amendments to the Constitution: (1) Freedom of speech, press, religion, assembly, and petition; (2) Right to bear arms; (3) No quartering of soldiers; (4) No unreasonable search and seizure; (5) Due process of law; (6) Right to a speedy trial; (7) Right to a jury trial in civil cases; (8) No cruel and unusual punishment; (9) Rights not enumerated in the Constitution are still protected; (10) Powers not given to the federal government are reserved for the states

events.title: Republican Motherhood
events.description: idea that women had vital role in shaping nation by raising virtuous citizens

events.title: First Bank of the United States is established
events.description: Federal Bank proposed by Alexander Hamilton to stabilize the economy and establish credit; to have all the states debts to one national debt, viewed as a control of power by opponents; helped by Elastic Clause in the Constitution

events.title: Hamilton (Fed) vs Jefferson (Dem-Rep)
events.description: Hamilton pushed for national debt, interest of rich, home manufacturing, strong executive, weak state government, and alliance with Britain; Jefferson pushed for government run by people, strong state governments, and was against a standing army

events.title: Whiskey Rebellion
events.description: Farmers in Pennsylvania rebelled against excise tax on whiskey; Washington sent troops to put down rebellion, expressing power of the new government; mainly supported by Federalists

events.title: Jay Treaty
events.description: Settle disputes between U.S. and Britain over trade and territory; U.S. will not trade with ports opened during war time that were closed during peace time, British will leave forts in the Northwest (completed by 1796) and allow U.S. trade in Asia

events.title: Washington's Farewell Address
events.description: Advised for strong central government, foreign neutrality, and warns against factions

events.title: John Adams elected, Jefferson as VP
events.description: George Washington steps down after two terms

events.title: XYZ Affair
events.description: France attacks American Ships and makes unreasonable demands—no money, no war

events.title: Alien and Sedition Acts
events.description: illegal to publish anything against government or president

events.title: Virginia and Kentucky Resolutions
events.description: gave states the right to nullify if deemed unconstitutional (ie. Alien and Sedition Acts)

events.title: Fries Uprising
events.description: opposed federal tax on property but was put down

events.title: Logan Act
events.description: George Logan attempts to negotiate with France, but deemed that a citizen cannot represent the government

events.title: Convention of 1800
events.description: Adams's peace commission negotiated with France, ended alliance with France during revolution, but extended "most-favored" trading status

units.summary: Political parties and foreign policies, debates about federal power, and the cultural and economic development of early America

presidents.name: Thomas Jefferson
presidents.description: argument between political parties, Supreme Court establishes its role, and U.S. expands territorial holdings

presidents.name: James Madison
presidents.description: led the nation during the War of 1812 and held commitment to civil liberties

presidents.name: James Monroe
presidents.description: Beginning of Era of Good Feelings

presidents.name: John Quincy Adams
presidents.description: Tariffs and debates on slavery

presidents.name: Andrew Jackson
presidents.description: Tariffs and banks

presidents.name: Martin Van Buren
presidents.description: Overspeculation of land and anti-bank

presidents.name: William Henry Harrison
presidents.description: Beginning of Antebellum Period, died

presidents.name: John Tyler
presidents.description: Did some stuff

presidents.name: James K. Polk
presidents.description: Admission of new states

events.title: Jefferson elected
events.description: government changes from Federalist to Democratic-Republican

events.title: Strict interpretation of the Constitution
events.description: Federalists supported loose interpretation of the Constitution; Democratic-Republicans supported strict interpretation of the Constitution to limit federal authority

events.title: Louisiana Purchase
events.description: Purchased most of middle from France after Napoleon failed to retake Haiti and needed money for war with Britain; Federalists opposed, established loose construction of the Constitution

events.title: Marbury v. Madison
events.description: Supreme Court declares parts of Judiciary Act of 1789 unconstitutional; Supreme Court could declare laws unconstitutional; powers of Court only given in Constitution

events.title: New Jersey passes gradual emancipation
events.description: last Northern state to begin gradual emancipation; slavery lingered in New Jersey until the Thirteenth Amendment (1865)

events.title: Lewis and Clark Expedition
events.description: Explored new territory after Louisiana Purchase; mapped uncharted land, brought details of Native Americans, and documented over 300 new species of animals and plants

events.title: Tripoli War ends
events.description: War between US and North African state of Tripoli; US refused to pay in 1801 which led to US ships being captured

events.title: First commercially successful steamboat
events.description: Robert Fulton's Clermont becomes the first commercially successful steamboat, reducing travel time significantly, stimulating economy through transportation of goods, and contributed to expansion westward

events.title: Chesapeake Affair
events.description: British ship HMS Leopard fired on the USS Chesapeake after it refused to be searched, killing three and seizing four sailors; provoked wave of nationalism and anti-British sentiment

events.title: Embargo Act
events.description: stopped trade exports to all foreign nations, put measures against impressment, placed import restrictions on Great Britain; led to economic hardship and made many resort to smuggling goods

events.title: African Slave Trade ends
events.description: transatlantic slave-trade abolished in the United States, however slaving continued to be legal

events.title: Madison elected
events.description: Madison had previously served as Secretary of States

events.title: Nonintercourse Act
events.description: resumes all trade barred during Embargo Act except with France and Britain

events.title: Fletcher v. Peck
events.description: action of a state can be declared unconstitutional

events.title: Charter for Bank of U.S. rejected
events.description: main debate between pro-bank Federalists and anti-centralized power Democratic-Republicans; many believed it favored elites

events.title: Battle of Tippecanoe
events.description: battle between Tecumseh's Indian confederacy, led in his absence by his brother Tenskwatawa (the Prophet) and supplied by the British, and Americans led by Harrison; destroyed hope for large Indian Confederacy

events.title: War Hawks
events.description: members of congress who pushed for war against Britain leading up to the War of 1812

events.title: The War of 1812
events.description: fought between U.S. and Great Britain; affirmed American independence from British influence, surge in nationalism; Federalists opposed the war, leading to decline in Federalist Party post-war

events.title: Treaty of Ghent
events.description: ended War of 1812; addressed territory of both parties, did not address trade restrictions and impressment of American sailors; paved way for Era of Good Feelings

events.title: Hartford Convention
events.description: Federalists were against War of 1812 and mercantile practice of Madison; secretly debated and rejected secession; drafted amendments strengthening state over commerce and militia

events.title: Second Bank of the United States created
events.description: created to stabilize economy after War of 1812 by regulating currency and managing federal funds

events.title: First Protective Tariff
events.description: to protect New England manufactures from cheap British manufactured goods

events.title: American Colonization Society founded
events.description: formed over debate of slavery and abolitionism; wanted relocate free blacks to Liberia, although many blacks at the time were born in the United States

events.title: Henry Clay's American System
events.description: to unify American by strengthen national economy through national bank, protective tariffs, and internal improvements, such as roads and canals

events.title: Monroe elected
events.description: marked start of Era of Good Feelings

events.title: Era of Good Feelings
events.description: decline of partisan conflicts; aimed to promote national unity and cooperation, economic growth, and territorial expansion; significant regional tensions between North and South over slavery

events.title: Veto of Bonus Bill
events.description: supplying funds for roads and canals to states; vetoed by Madison, as he believed the Constitution did not allow federal funding for internal improvements without an amendment

events.title: Rush-Bagot Disarmament
events.description: agreement between U.S. and Britain; aimed to limit naval armaments on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain to de-escalate tensions between the two nations

events.title: Convention of 1818
events.description: set boundary between the Missouri Territory and British North America at the forty-ninth parallel; marked beginning of Anglo-American cooperation

events.title: Transcontinental Treaty/Adams-Onis Treaty
events.description: U.S. acquired Florida from Spain for 5 million, put boundary to Spanish territories, later Texas, New Mexico, and California

events.title: Panic of 1819
events.description: first major financial crisis of the U.S.; widespread economic downturn and bank failures, which led to scrutiny of banking practices and reform of banking system; rise of populism and changing attitudes of government intervention into economy

events.title: McCulloch v Maryland
events.description: federal government had the right to set up a federal bank and the states did not have the power to tax the government

events.title: Dartmouth College v Woodward
events.description: Dartmouth charter as private could not be changed to public by the New Hampshire legislature; established principle of protecting private corporations from state interference

events.title: Missouri Compromise
events.description: admitted Maine as a free state and Missouri as a slave state but no slavery in the rest of the Louisiana Territory north of the 36°30′ line

events.title: Cumberland Road Bill
events.description: bill to collect tolls to repair the Cumberland Road was vetoed by Monroe as unconstitutional; Cumberland Road, or the National Road, was the first federally funded highway; helped in the Market Revolution and facilitated westward expansion; made precedent for federal involvement in infrastructure and future transportation projects

events.title: Monroe Doctrine
events.description: foreign policy statement that warned European nations against colonization and intervention in the Americas and established the Western Hemisphere as the sphere of American influence; set commitment to protecting Latin American nations; established U.S. as a growing global power

events.title: Russo-American Treaty
events.description: outlined boundaries between U.S. and Russian Alaska

events.title: John Q. Adams elected
events.description: defeats Andrew Jackson and Clay; Andrew Jackson received most popular and electoral votes; House elected John Quincy Adams after allegedly striking a deal with Henry Clay who had received the least of the four candidates, sparking accusations of a 'Corrupt Bargain'

events.title: Gibbons v. Ogden
events.description: concluded that interstate trade would be regulated by Congress under the Commerce Clause, not by the states

events.title: Erie Canal opens
events.description: first transportation route connecting the Atlantic Ocean and the Great Lakes that did not require over land transportation

events.title: Panama Conference (PAN American)
events.description: meeting of Latin American nations called by Simón Bolívar; U.S. delegates never took part (one died on the way and the other arrived too late) after a long debate in Congress; the Pan-American Union was not formed until much later (1889-1910)

events.title: Tariff of Abominations
events.description: significant tariffs on imported goods and raw materials; greatly opposed by Southern economy

events.title: South Carolina Exposition and Protest
events.description: Calhoun protests for and reaffirms the rights of states to nullify

events.title: Andrew Jackson elected
events.description: Jackson promises to limit executive power, provide internal improvements, and lower debt; appoints 'Kitchen Cabinet' of trusted friends

events.title: Maysville Road Bill Veto
events.description: proposed building a road in Kentucky, but vetoed as Jackson didn't like Clay and Martin Van Buren noted New York and Pennsylvania paid for their transportation with state money; applied strict interpretation of the Constitution

events.title: Webster-Hayne Debates
events.description: Webster (nationalist) and Hayne (states rights) debated on the topic nullification

events.title: Transcendentalism
events.description: emphasized individual intuition, inherent goodness of people, and a deeper connection to nature; promoted self-reliance and questioned social norms

events.title: The Second Great Awakening
events.description: religious revival movement in the early 19th century; included renewed interest in Christianity, increase in church membership, and formation of various new religious denominations; brought early feminism and other reform movements

events.title: Baltimore and Ohio Railroad begins operation
events.description: first common carrier railroad in the U.S. to provide transportation between the East Coast and the Ohio River

events.title: The Liberator begins publication
events.description: abolitionist movement becomes more widespread; served as important part of Boston's Underground Railroad network and reported on fugitive slave cases; the South were highly against, due to their reliance on slaves for economy

events.title: Nat Turner Rebellion
events.description: bloody slave rebellion in Virginia that led to killings of nearly 60 white people; caused black churches to be broken up, Anti-literacy laws to increase, and put harsher restrictions on slaves and blacks

events.title: Cyrus McCormick invents the reaper
events.description: made cutting crops for harvest much more efficient

events.title: The Trail of Tears
events.description: about 60,000 Southern Indians forcefully removed from their homelands in the Southeast and sent to designated Indian Territory (present-day Oklahoma) west of the Mississippi, causing death of many Indians due to disease and starvation

events.title: Tariff of 1832
events.description: to act as a remedy for Tariff of 1828; reduced duties but retained high taxes on imported irons, cottons, and woolens; led to the nullification crisis

events.title: Ordinance of Nullification
events.description: South Carolina refused to accept the tariff as the believed it would set a precedent for congressional legislation for slavery; made it unlawful for federal officials to collect duties in state

events.title: Force Bill
events.description: made in response to the Southern nullification and allowed the president to use force as necessary to enforce tariffs

events.title: Veto of Bank of U.S. recharter
events.description: Jackson vetos recharter just before reelection of 1832, stating it was unconstitutional despite being considered constitutional by the court, placed Federal funds in banks that supported Jackson and state banks

events.title: Department of Indian affairs established
events.description: Congress created the position of Commissioner of Indian Affairs within the War Department to manage federal relations with Native Americans during the era of Indian removal

events.title: Seminole War with Indians begins
events.description: Second Seminole War; Seminoles in Florida, led by Osceola and joined by escaped slaves, resisted removal under the Treaty of Payne's Landing (1832); fighting lasted until 1842, the longest and costliest of the Indian wars; most Seminoles were eventually removed to Indian Territory

events.title: Cherokee Nation v. Georgia
events.description: Supreme Court ruled that the Cherokee were a 'domestic dependent nation' rather than a foreign nation, so the Court could not hear their suit against Georgia; in Worcester v. Georgia (1832) the Court ruled Georgia law did not apply on Cherokee land, but Jackson refused to enforce the decision

events.title: Agreement with Britain to open West Indies ports
events.description: Jackson's administration reached an agreement reopening the British West Indies to direct trade with American ships, which had long been restricted; a diplomatic success for Jackson

events.title: Texas War of Independence
events.description: rebellion by Texas settlers against Mexican rule, leading to establishment of Republic of Texas; 'Lone Star Republic'

events.title: The Gag Rule
events.description: prohibited debate or action on anti-slavery petitions; reflected increasing tensions around slavery

events.title: Specie Circular
events.description: required that western land must be paid with hard currency; caused failure of banks as banks did not have that much hard currency

events.title: Van Buren elected
events.description: successor to Jackson, Martin Van Buren beats Harrison (Whigs) but is 'puppet' of Jackson

events.title: Recognition of Republic of Texas
events.description: one year after Texas declares independence from Mexico

events.title: Oberlin College enrolls first women students
events.description: early steps of feminism movement

events.title: Charles River Bridge v. Warren Bridge
events.description: strict interpretation of contract; narrowed Dartmouth College v. Woodward by ruling that the community's interest outweighs rights not clearly stated in a charter

events.title: Panic of 1837
events.description: financial crisis caused by rapid economic growth, speculation of land, and concerns of banks

events.title: Aroostook War
events.description: bloodless boundary disputes between Maine and New Brunswick

events.title: Independent Treasury Systems
events.description: constructs vaults to hold federal money rather than have commercial banks manage funds as response to economic instability

events.title: Harrison elected
events.description: Harrison defeats Van Buren

events.title: Tyler becomes president
events.description: Harrison catches pneumonia and dies

events.title: Independent Treasury Act repealed
events.description: Whigs repealed it because they wanted to replace it with a new national bank

events.title: Recharter of Bank of the U.S. vetoed
events.description: Tyler vetoes recharter to charter a new National Bank to replace

events.title: Preemption Bill
events.description: to protect rights of 'squatters,' settlers who occupied public lands before they were surveyed and sold by the government, to allow claiming land before it was surveyed

events.title: Tariff Bill of 1842/Black Tariff
events.description: raised tariffs back to how it was in 1832, reversing Compromise Tariff of 1833 to protect American industries from foreign competition

events.title: Dorr Rebellion
events.description: rebellion in Rhode Island against land qualifications needed for voting; put down by the state militia, as Tyler promised federal support but did not send troops

events.title: Webster-Ashburton Treaty
events.description: resolved border disputes between British North America and the United States; also addressed African slave trade and extradition

events.title: Oregon Trail
events.description: route used to reach Oregon Territory and other westward areas

events.title: Polk elected
events.description: Polk (Dem) defeats Clay (Whig) and Birney (Liberty; Anti-slavery)

events.title: Texas Annexation Bill
events.description: joint resolution of Congress allowed annexation of Texas, leading to Texas's admission as a state later in the year

units.summary: Manifest Destiny, Mexican-American War, Southern Secession, and the leading to the Civil War

presidents.name: James K. Polk
presidents.description: Admission of new states

presidents.name: Zachary Taylor
presidents.description: Died in office

presidents.name: Millard Fillmore
presidents.description: Truce over battle of slavery

presidents.name: Franklin Pierce
presidents.description: Kansas-Nebraska Act and rising sectional conflict

presidents.name: James Buchanan
presidents.description: Beginning of Southern Secession and Civil War

presidents.name: Abraham Lincoln
presidents.description: Led Union through the Civil War

presidents.name: Andrew Johnson
presidents.description: Reconstruction after the Civil War

presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
presidents.description: War general turned president

events.title: Polk elected
events.description: Polk (Dem) defeats Clay (Whig) and Birney (Liberty; Anti-slavery)

events.title: Manifest Destiny
events.description: term coined by journalist John O'Sullivan for the belief that Americans were destined by God to spread democracy and settle the continent from coast to coast; used to justify the annexation of Texas, the Oregon claims, and the Mexican-American War

events.title: Elias Howe invents sewing machine
events.description: revolutionized clothing industry and boosted Northern industrialization during the Industrial Revolution

events.title: Mexican-American War
events.description: stemming from the annexation of Texas, the war represents growing expansionism and forced American's to discuss the issue of slavery

events.title: Slidell Mission
events.description: to negotiate purchase of California and New Mexico; arrival marked with hostility

events.title: Wilmot Proviso
events.description: proposed to ban slavery in any territory acquired from Mexican-American War; never made a law but contributed to the rise of the Free Soil Party and the Republican Party who were against slavery

events.title: Fifty-four Forty or Fight
events.description: a popular slogan used during the Oregon Question; American's wanted the land about 54 degrees and 40 minutes north parallel or would fight Great Britain for the land

events.title: Reestablishment of the Independent Treasury System
events.description: to separate federal government's funds from private banks and manage them through the Treasury instead

events.title: Walker Tariff Act
events.description: lowered import duties in the U.S., aiming to reduce since Black Tariff; led to increase in trade and government revenue

events.title: Polk Doctrine
events.description: resurrection of the Monroe Doctrine; warned European powers not to interfere with U.S. expansion in North America, such as Texas, Oregon, and California

events.title: Obtained Oregon
events.description: for years, Oregon Territory had been joint owned by the U.S. and Britain; the Oregon Treaty split it at the 49th parallel; major part of Manifest Destiny ideology

events.title: Trist Mission
events.description: negotiates Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo to get territory of Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming

events.title: Gold Rush in California
events.description: Gold discovered in Sutter's Mill, California led many to migrate to California in hopes of striking it rich; led to rapid westward migration and political and economic changes

events.title: Seneca Falls Women's Rights Convention
events.description: first women's rights convention aiming for women suffrage

events.title: Taylor elected
events.description: Taylor (Whig) defeats Cass (Dem; father of popular sovereignty) and Van Buren (Free-Soil; against expansion of slavery)

events.title: Fillmore becomes president
events.description: Taylor dies

events.title: Clay's Compromise of 1850
events.description: crafted by three influential statesmen, Henry Clay, Daniel Webster, and Stephen Douglas; passed as five separate bills: California as a free state, strong Fugitive Slave Act, End to slave trade in Washington D.C., Texas/New Mexico boundary settled, popular sovereignty in Utah and New Mexico territories

events.title: Clayton-Bulwer Treaty
events.description: U.S. amd Britain agree to jointly protect the neutrality of a canal in Central America

events.title: Japan opens to US trade
events.description: Fillmore sent Commodore Matthew Perry, who reached Japan in 1853 and demanded opening of trade to the US; Treaty of Kanagawa (1854) opened Japanese ports

events.title: Pierce elected
events.description: Pierce defeats Scott (Whig)

events.title: Gadsden Purchase
events.description: purchase land from Mexico to build transcontinental railroad and exhibited America's Manifest Destiny

events.title: 'Uncle Tom's Cabin'
events.description: anti-slavery novel written by Harriet Beecher Stowe; helped shape Northern perceptions of African American slavery

events.title: Kansas-Nebraska Act
events.description: repealed the Missouri Compromise and created two new territories that allowed for popular sovereignty; produced a violent uprising known as 'Bleeding Kansas' where proslavery and antislavery activists flooded in to sway the vote

events.title: New England Emigrant Aid Society
events.description: helped people emigrate into Kansas and Nebraska territories

events.title: Republican Party founded
events.description: formed in opposition to the Kansas-Nebraska Act by Free Soilers, antislavery 'Conscience' Whigs, and antislavery Democrats; opposed the expansion of slavery into the territories; replaced the collapsing Whig Party as the second major party

events.title: Know-Nothing Party
events.description: nativist American Party that opposed Irish and German Catholic immigrants, whose numbers surged in the 1840s and 1850s due to the Irish Potato Famine and failed German revolutions; won many local offices in 1854-1855 but split over slavery

events.title: Bleeding Kansas
events.description: Topeka government (Free Soil) against LeCompton government (slavery) in Kansas to determine slave status of state

events.title: Ostend Manifesto
events.description: secret memo by American diplomats urging the U.S. to buy Cuba from Spain and justifying seizing it by force if Spain refused; resulted from debates over slavery, where slaveholders wanted a new territory for expansion of slavery; northerners were outraged by Southerners

events.title: Walker expedition
events.description: Walker raises an army and takes over Nicaragua to develop a proslavery empire; Pierce recognizes the new government, but Walker was killed by Honduran authorities

events.title: Lawrence Mob Violence
events.description: burned many abolitionist materials

events.title: Caning of Charles Sumner
events.description: Representative Preston Brooks of South Carolina beat Senator Charles Sumner with a cane on the Senate floor after Sumner's 'Crime Against Kansas' speech; Brooks was hailed as a hero in the South, showing the deepening sectional divide

events.title: Pottawatomie Massacre
events.description: John Brown and his followers kill five pro-slavery settlers; John Brown believed that violent action was necessary to combat slavery; ended up further polarizing public opinion about slavery

events.title: Buchanan elected
events.description: Buchanan defeats Fremont (Rep; Free Soil) and Fillmore (Know Nothings)

events.title: Dred Scott decision
events.description: slaves are property that can be taken anywhere; cannot be freed from staying into slave-free state; ruled that Black Americans were not citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories, making the Missouri Compromise unconstitutional; Northerners feared it could lead to slavery in the North

events.title: LeCompton Constitution
events.description: proposed constitution for the state of Kansas during territorial disputes over slavery; wanted to establish Kansas as a slave state but became symbol of failure regarding expansion of slavery

events.title: Panic of 1857
events.description: North was heavily invested in industries that caused the panic but the South were more reliant on shipping and foreign economy; emboldened South that slavery was good for economy and made a false sense of security that they would succeed as a country

events.title: Lincoln-Douglas Debates
events.description: a series of seven debates between Abraham Lincoln and Stephen A. Douglas mostly on the extension of slavery into new territories; Lincoln prompted moral issues of slavery, while Douglas promoted popular sovereignty; Douglas won reelection to senate but Lincoln gained national recognition

events.title: Freeport Doctrine
events.description: asserted that territories could effectively exclude slavery by not adopting laws to protect it

events.title: 'a house divided against itself cannot stand
events.description: Lincoln emphasized that unity was essential and nation could not be permanently half slave and half free; after Lincoln's election, many Southerners believed their way of life was under threat

events.title: John Brown's Raid on Harpers Ferry
events.description: armed attack by John Brown to seize federal armory and spark a slave uprising; Brown was captured during the raid and tried for treason against Virginia, and was executed on December 2nd

events.title: Crittenden Compromise
events.description: unsuccessful proposal to make it unconstitutional for future congress to end slavery

events.title: Lincoln elected
events.description: Lincoln defeats Douglas (Dem), but not on a abolitionist stance

events.title: Civil War
events.description: debates over slavery caused Southern secession and war between Union (North) and Confederates (South)

events.title: 'necessity knows no law'
events.description: Lincoln increases army and navy, creates first income tax, creates greenbacks, removes freedom of press or speech

events.title: Confederacy established
events.description: Davis as president, weak government as many Southerners disliked strong government; no protective tariffs, no federal funded improvements, states could impeach federal officers, state supreme, protection of slavery, and 2/3 of house to appropriate money

events.title: Kansas admitted as a free state
events.description: anti-slavery forces in Kansas was more significant

events.title: Attack on Fort Sumter
events.description: Confederate forces fired on the federal fort in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, starting the Civil War; Lincoln called for volunteers, leading Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee, and North Carolina to secede; border slave states (Delaware, Maryland, Kentucky, Missouri) stayed in the Union

events.title: Ex parte Merryman
events.description: Lincoln suspends habeas corpus (allowed detention of individuals) and passes martial law in Maryland; Chief Justice Taney ruled that only Congress could suspend habeas corpus, but Lincoln ignored the ruling

events.title: Battle of Bull Run
events.description: South victory ends up extending the Civil War

events.title: Pacific Railroad Act
events.description: partially federally funded railroad and gave land for railroad; received little resistance as the South had seceded

events.title: Homestead Act
events.description: gave 160 acres of public land in the West to settlers who lived on and farmed it for five years; encouraged westward settlement

events.title: Morrill Land-Grant College Act
events.description: government land grants for agricultural college to promote agricultural growth

events.title: Battle of Antietam
events.description: aftermath led Lincoln to issue Emancipation Proclamation, changing focus of war to include slavery and dissuaded Britain and France from recognizing the Confederacy

events.title: Banking Acts
events.description: established federally chartered banks; was possible due to little resistance of the South that had seceded

events.title: Draft Riot in New York
events.description: over unfair burden of poor as rich could get out of drafts; significant violence, particularly of working-class Irish immigrants, fearing their jobs would be taken by freed African Americans if they were conscripted

events.title: Emancipation Proclamation
events.description: declared that all persons held as slaves in rebellious states to be free

events.title: Battle of Gettysburg
events.description: turning point to Union strength in war; largest number of casualties in th entire war, where Robert E. Lee of the Confederates made an ambitious quest to invade the north but was cut down

events.title: Fall of Vicksburg
events.description: Ulysses S. Grant captured Vicksburg after a siege, giving the Union control of the Mississippi River and splitting the Confederacy in two, fulfilling a key goal of the Anaconda Plan

events.title: Gettysburg Address
events.description: Lincoln's short speech at the dedication of the Gettysburg battlefield cemetery redefined the war as a struggle for a 'new birth of freedom' and government 'of the people, by the people, for the people'

events.title: '10 Percent Plan'
events.description: Lincoln proposed a reconstruction program that would allow the Southern states to be readmitted once ten percent of its voters took an oath of allegiance to the Union; offered a lenient path for reestablishment and reconciliation

events.title: Lincoln is reelected
events.description: defeats McClellan (Dem), a previous officer who had worked under Lincoln but was fired multiple times after failures

events.title: Wade-Davis Bill
events.description: divided South ito military units until majority pledges allegiance and bans slavery; with Wade-Davis Manifesto that suggested Congress controlled reconstruction

events.title: Sand Creek Massacre
events.description: Chivington attacks defenseless Indian village, many of whom wre women and children; highlights violet conflicts and culture tensions during westward expansion

events.title: Sherman's March to the Sea
events.description: after capturing Atlanta (helping Lincoln's reelection), General William T. Sherman marched to Savannah, destroying railroads, crops, and property; 'total war' aimed at breaking the South's economy and will to fight

events.title: Civil War ends
events.description: Civil War effectively ended as Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered to Union General Ulysses s. Grant at Appomattox Court House in Virginia; firmly demonstrated the strength of the U.S. government and restored legitimacy to handle sectional tensions

events.title: Freedmen's Bureau
events.description: federal agency to assist newly freed slaves in the South after the Civil War by providing food, housing, education, and medical care; Souther whites resisted its policies and undermined its authority with violence and intimidation

events.title: Andrew Johnson becomes president
events.description: Lincoln is assassinated at Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth, becoming the first president to be assassinated in office; led many to blame South who were bitter of loss

events.title: Johnson's amnesty plan
events.description: pardons almost all Confederates who had directly or indirectly taken part in the rebellion and restored all rights of property except slaves

events.title: Thirteenth Amendment
events.description: formally abolishes slavery in its entirety, even in the North

events.title: Black Codes
events.description: laws passed by Southern states to restrict freedpeople: limited property ownership, required yearly labor contracts, and vagrancy laws allowed forced labor; angered Northerners and pushed Congress toward Radical Reconstruction

events.title: Ku Klux Klan founded
events.description: secret white supremacist society founded by Confederate veterans in Tennessee; used violence and intimidation against freedpeople and Republicans to undermine Reconstruction; suppressed by the Force Acts (1870-1871)

events.title: Civil Rights Act of 1866
events.description: declared all persons born in the U.S. (except untaxed Native Americans) to be citizens with equal rights under the law; first major law passed over a presidential veto (Johnson)

events.title: Fourteenth Amendment
events.description: passed by Congress in 1866 and ratified in 1868; granted citizenship to all persons born or naturalized in the U.S. and required states to guarantee due process and equal protection of the laws; Southern states had to ratify it to be readmitted; later basis for many civil rights cases

events.title: Radical Republicans take control of Congress
events.description: Radical Republicans like Thaddeus Stevens and Charles Sumner, who wanted to protect freedpeople's rights and transform Southern society, won large majorities in the 1866 midterm elections and took control of Reconstruction from Johnson

events.title: Reconstruction Acts
events.description: divided the South (except Tennessee) into five military districts; Southern states had to ratify the Fourteenth Amendment and guarantee Black male suffrage in new state constitutions to be readmitted

events.title: Tenure of Office Act
events.description: required Senate approval for the president to remove Cabinet officials; Johnson's firing of Secretary of War Edwin Stanton led to his impeachment

events.title: Purchase of Alaska
events.description: Secretary of State William Seward bought Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million; mocked as 'Seward's Folly' but later found rich in resources

events.title: Johnson impeached
events.description: House impeached Andrew Johnson for violating the Tenure of Office Act; Senate acquitted him by one vote, leaving him in office but politically powerless

events.title: Sharecropping
events.description: labor system in which landless farmers (many freedpeople and poor whites) worked land owned by others in exchange for a share of the crop; the crop-lien system trapped many in cycles of debt

events.title: Grant elected
events.description: Grant (Rep) defeats Seymour (Dem); votes of newly enfranchised Black men in the South helped Grant win the popular vote

events.title: Panic of 1873
events.description: economic depression triggered by the collapse of Jay Cooke's banking firm and railroad overbuilding; shifted Northern attention away from Reconstruction toward economic problems

events.title: Redeemers
events.description: Southern Democrats who regained control of state governments from Republicans through elections, intimidation, and violence; 'redemption' of the South was completed after federal troops withdrew in 1877

units.summary: Economic and demographic shifts of the nation, settlement in the West, the "New South," reform movements, and debates about government role

presidents.name: Andrew Johnson
presidents.description: Led through black rights movements and KKK

presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
presidents.description: Made successful foreign policy and improved Anglo-American relations

presidents.name: Rutherford B. Hayes
presidents.description: Brought forth the Gilded Age

presidents.name: James A. Garfield
presidents.description: Assassinated

presidents.name: Chester A. Arthur
presidents.description: Expansion of the U.S. Navy, end of the spoils system, and harsher immigration restrictions

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
presidents.description: Period of unrest with labor unions

presidents.name: Benjamin Harrison
presidents.description: Played into foreign affairs and westward expansion

events.title: The Grange (Patrons of Husbandry)
events.description: farmers' organization founded by Oliver Kelley as a social and educational group that turned political; pushed Midwestern states to pass Granger laws regulating railroad and grain elevator rates, upheld in Munn v. Illinois (1877)

events.title: Grant elected
events.description: Grant defeats Seymour (Dem)

events.title: Transcontinental Railroad Completed from Union Pacific and Central Pacific
events.description: allowed easier transportation from west to east and helped with further westward expansion and settlement

events.title: Knights of Labor
events.description: one of the most prominent labor unions but ended quickly; included all people of different work levels

events.title: Fifteenth Amendment
events.description: rights to vote cannot be determined by race or color; allowed black men to vote, but did not give women vote yet

events.title: Force Acts
events.description: to protect the constitutional rights guaranteed to blacks by the fourteenth and fifteenth amendments

events.title: Standard Oil Company
events.description: Standard Oil Company was founded by John D. Rockefeller and organized as a trust in 1882; used horizontal integration, buying out or driving out competing refineries until it controlled about 90% of oil refining

events.title: Political machines and Boss Tweed
events.description: urban political machines like New York's Tammany Hall traded jobs and services to immigrants for votes while stealing public money through graft; Boss William Tweed was exposed by Thomas Nast's cartoons and convicted in 1873

events.title: Credit Mobilier Scandal
events.description: stock holders of railroad construction company overcharge the government for a job

events.title: Grant reelected
events.description: Grant gets reelected against Greeley (Liberal Republican, endorsed by Democrats)

events.title: Slaughterhouse Cases
events.description: represent Court's first major interpretation of the Fourteenth Amendment; Fourteenth Amendment did not concern monopolies, thus giving it a narrower interpretation

events.title: Red River Wars
events.description: last major attempt of Southern Plains tribes (Comanche, Kiowa, and Southern Cheyenne) to resist reservations

events.title: Civil Rights Act
events.description: gave blacks equal rights; aimed to guarantee equal access to public accommodations; was not very successful as it was not enforced as much

events.title: Carnegie's steel empire
events.description: Andrew Carnegie opened his first steel mill using the Bessemer process and built an empire through vertical integration, controlling every stage from iron ore and coal to railroads and mills; sold to J.P. Morgan in 1901 to form U.S. Steel

events.title: Battle of Little Bighorn
events.description: a battle in the Great Sioux War of 1876; resulted in a Native American win with Custer and forces killed

events.title: U.S. v. Reese
events.description: over voting qualifications to prevent black sufferage and whether Congress should enforce the Fifteenth Amendment; allowed South to impliment discriminatory acts such as literacy tests, poll tax, and the grandfather clause

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell invents the telephone
events.description: allowed for easier long distance communication, helping facilitate railroad businesses and westward expansion

events.title: Hayes elected
events.description: Hayes defeats Tilden (Dem)

events.title: Munn v. Illinois
events.description: over state regulation of prices; if it is in the interest of public good, then states can regulate prices to a reasonable extent

events.title: Robber Barons
events.description: Tipple: believed it threatened traditional beliefs and destroyed competition; Chandler: that entrepreneurs were hard working and innovative; Arnold: that anti-trust acts preserved competition; McGraw: that regulation was inefficient

events.title: Social Darwinism
events.description: Herbert Spencer and William Graham Sumner applied 'survival of the fittest' to society, arguing that the wealthy deserved their success; used to justify laissez-faire economics, wealth inequality, and opposition to government aid for the poor

events.title: Compromise of 1877
events.description: informal agreement between Southern Democrats and allies of Hayes; marked the end of the Reconstruction era

events.title: Great Railroad Strike of 1877
events.description: first nationwide strike, begun by railroad workers protesting wage cuts; spread to many cities with rioting; Hayes sent federal troops to end it, and about 100 people were killed

events.title: Nez Perce War
events.description: the Nez Perce fled U.S. troops trying to force them onto a reservation, traveling over 1,000 miles; Chief Joseph surrendered near the Canadian border ('I will fight no more forever')

events.title: Farmers Alliance
events.description: farmers' organization formed in Texas that spread across the South and Great Plains, fighting high railroad rates and crop-lien debt through cooperatives; later helped form the Populist Party (Granger laws came earlier from the Grange)

events.title: Hall v. Decuir
events.description: states cannot regulate segregation on common carriers for interstate commerce; struck down Louisiana law requiring full racial integration of passengers; limited the scopes of Civil Rights Act of 1875

events.title: Bland-Allison Act
events.description: coined a limited number of silver; aimed to combat economic downturns; exemplified rift between farmers who struggled with debt and deflation and industrialists who favored a gold standard

events.title: Treaty of 1878
events.description: treaty of friendship and commerce with Samoa and gave naval station at Pago Pago; represented growing imperialism

events.title: Thomas Edison invents the electric light
events.description: shift towards electricty from common gas usage; allowed longer work hours in industry

events.title: Exodusters
events.description: thousands of African Americans migrated from the South to Kansas to escape violence, sharecropping debt, and the end of Reconstruction

events.title: Garfield elected
events.description: defeats Hancock (Dem)

events.title: Arthur becomes president
events.description: Garfield dies, VP Chester Arthur becomes president

events.title: Tuskegee Institute
events.description: industrial school led by Booker T. Washington to train young black students and improve their economic status

events.title: A Century of Dishonor
events.description: Helen Hunt Jackson wrote about Native American view and settlers disregards of Native American rights and cultures; contributed to policy reforms over Native American tribes

events.title: Knights of Labor go public
events.description: dropped their secrecy under leader Terence Powderly; no strike stand; both skilled and unskilled labor made it generally unsuccessful

events.title: Chinese Exclusion Act
events.description: the first major U.S. law to restrict immigration bsed on race and nationality; prohibited the immigration Chinese laborers and denied naturalization of Chinese residents; fueled by economic competition and racial prejudice

events.title: Immigration Act of 1882
events.description: imposed head tax on non-citizens and restricted certain people from entering the country, mainly those unable to care for themselvecs or with criminal background

events.title: Brooklyn Bridge
events.description: connected Manhattan and Broklyn to be the longest suspension bridge in the world; represented American technology and commercial advancement

events.title: Civil Rights Cases
events.description: series of five cases that struck down the Civil Rights Act of 1875 and allowed individual discrimination; was accompanied by more Jim Crow laws

events.title: Pendleton Civil Service Act
events.description: passed after Garfield was assassinated by a disappointed office-seeker; required competitive exams for many federal jobs and banned forcing officeholders to make political contributions; weakened the spoils system

events.title: New South
events.description: Henry Grady promoted a 'New South' of industry (textiles, tobacco, and iron and steel in Birmingham) and railroads; yet the South remained largely agricultural and poor, dependent on sharecropping and Northern capital

events.title: Jim Crow laws
events.description: state and local laws enforcing racial segregation in the South in schools, transportation, and public facilities; backed by disenfranchisement and the violence of lynching; upheld by Plessy v. Ferguson (1896)

events.title: Cleveland elected
events.description: Cleveland defeates Blaine (Rep)

events.title: The American Federation of Labor
events.description: composed of only skilled labor and dealt with labor using strikes; was more effective as skilled labor could not be easily replaced

events.title: Haymarket Incident
events.description: peaceful protest turned violent; changed public perception of labor unions, effectively ending the Knights of Labor

events.title: Interstate Commerce Act
events.description: regulated railroads' and private businesses' monopolistic practice, prohibiting rebates and preferences for localities; established Interstate Commerce Commission

events.title: Interstate Commerce Commission
events.description: oversaw railroads to ensure just and reasonable rates

events.title: Dawes Severalty Act
events.description: aimed to divide Native American reservations into individual land allotments and assimilate Native Americans into U.S. society, encouraging them to become independent farming and landowners; failed

events.title: Pearl Harbor acquired
events.description: renewal of the 1875 Reciprocity Treaty with Hawaii gave the U.S. exclusive rights to use Pearl Harbor as a naval base

events.title: Harrison elected
events.description: defeated Cleveland (Dem)

events.title: Jane Addams and Hull House
events.description: settlement house that aimed to help urban poor by providing services and advocating for social reform

events.title: Berlin Conference
events.description: U.S., Britain, and Germany agree on a joint protection of Samoa but does not work well

events.title: First Pan American Conference
events.description: to foster cooperation among American nations and established trade relations

events.title: Bering Sea Controversy
events.description: between U.S. and Britain (Canada) over seal hunting; led to capturing of Canadian vessels and led to arbitration

events.title: Gospel of Wealth
events.description: essay by Andrew Carnegie arguing that the wealthy had a duty to use their fortunes for the public good through philanthropy, such as funding libraries and universities

events.title: National American Woman Suffrage Association
events.description: fought for women suffrage; formed through merging two existing suffrage groups; helped secure the Nineteenth Amendment

events.title: How the Other Half Lives
events.description: Jacob Riis's photographs and writing exposed crowded, unsanitary tenement slums in New York City; spurred housing reform and influenced later muckrakers

events.title: Blacks deprived of suffrage in the South
events.description: against previous acts that allowed black rights

events.title: Ghost Dance movement
events.description: Native American religious movement promising the return of the buffalo and the departure of white settlers; alarmed U.S. officials on Lakota reservations, leading to the killing of Sitting Bull and the Wounded Knee Massacre

events.title: Wounded Knee Massacre
events.description: ended Indian Wars, shot and killed nearly 300 Lakota people

units.summary: America's changing society and culture, imperialism and global policy during the two wars, innovations, and combatting domestic problems

presidents.name: Woodrow Wilson
presidents.description: Progressive reforms and led the United States through World War I

presidents.name: Warren G. Harding
presidents.description: Return to normalcy after World War I

presidents.name: Calvin Coolidge
presidents.description: Anti-immigration

presidents.name: Herbert Hoover
presidents.description: Attempting to bring the U.S. through the Great Depression

presidents.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
presidents.description: Brought the Era of Reform through the New Deal and guided the U.S. through World War II

presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
presidents.description: Ended World War II

events.title: Sherman Antitrust Act
events.description: trust in restraint of trade are illegal; to prevent monopolies and promote competitions

events.title: Sherman Silver Purchase Act
events.description: government bought 4.5 million ounces of silver a month, paying with Treasury notes redeemable in gold or silver; meant to increase the money supply (inflation) to help indebted farmers, but drained the government's gold reserves

events.title: McKinley Tariff Act
events.description: raises tariffs on imported goods to protect American Industries from foreign competition

events.title: Homestead Strike
events.description: against Carnegie Steel, Pinkerton guards and troops put strike down; ended in loss for union and workers

events.title: Miner Strike in Idaho
events.description: miner strike against reduction of wages and increase of working hours

events.title: General Electric Company
events.description: major role in industrial revolution and electrical industry founded by Thomas Edison

events.title: Ellis Island opens
events.description: federal immigration station in New York Harbor that processed millions of 'new immigrants' from Southern and Eastern Europe (Italians, Poles, Russian Jews), who often faced nativist hostility; Angel Island (1910) in San Francisco Bay processed Asian immigrants

events.title: Ida B. Wells's anti-lynching campaign
events.description: journalist Ida B. Wells published Southern Horrors, exposing lynching as a tool of white supremacy rather than punishment for crimes; led a national and international anti-lynching crusade

events.title: Populist Omaha Platform
events.description: aimed for eight hour work day, nationalization of railroad, inflation, coinage of silver, direct election of senators, anti-rich capitalists, and decrease in tariff

events.title: Populists
events.description: Goodwyn: populists are democratic activists; Hicks: populists are rational people reacting to harsh laissez-faire; Hofstadter: anti-intellectuals fighting for a lost cause; Turner: West has major impact on American policies

events.title: Cleveland elected
events.description: Cleveland defeats Harrison (Rep) and Weaver (Populists)

events.title: Panic of 1893
events.description: economic depression that led to unemployment, bank failures, and failures in railroad industry

events.title: Sherman Silver Purchase Act repealed
events.description: aimed to stabilize the economy and restore confidence in the U.S. dollar; protected the government's shrinking gold reserves

events.title: Overthrow of the Hawaiian monarchy
events.description: American sugar planters led by Sanford Dole, backed by U.S. Marines, overthrew Queen Liliuokalani; Cleveland opposed annexation as improper, but Hawaii was annexed in 1898 under McKinley

events.title: Turner's Frontier Thesis
events.description: historian Frederick Jackson Turner argued the frontier had shaped American democracy and individualism, and that its closing (announced by the 1890 census) marked the end of an era; used by some to argue for overseas expansion

events.title: Pullman Strike
events.description: Pullman Company controls prices but fires workers; American Railway Union supported by boycotting Pullman cars, paralyzing rail traffic nationwide; led to federal government intervention and ultimate failure

events.title: Coxey's Army marches
events.description: goal for unemployment relief from government

events.title: U.S. v. E.C. Knight Company
events.description: ruled that Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 could not stop the American Sugar Refining Company's acquisition of E.C. Knight Co. even though it created a virtual monopoly; meant Congress could not regulate manufacturing monopolies

events.title: Pollock v. Farmers' Loan and Trust Co.
events.description: determined that income tax was unconstitutional

events.title: In re Debs
events.description: case court regarding federal governments's authority to use injunctions to prevent obstructions to interstate commerce; in response to Pullman Strike of 1894

events.title: Booker T. Washington's Atlanta Compromise Speech
events.description: declared that both races must accept and help each other, and that blacks had to earn their rights

events.title: Plessy v. Ferguson
events.description: upheld 'separate but equal' doctrine that allowed states to segregate public facilities as long as the provided separate but equal facilities for all races; eventually overturned in 1954 Brown v. Board

events.title: McKinley elected
events.description: defeats Bryan (Dem)

events.title: Dingley Tariff
events.description: raised tax on duties, reflected Republican economic policy

events.title: De Lôme Letter
events.description: private letter by the Spanish minister to the U.S. calling McKinley weak was published in Hearst's New York Journal; along with the sinking of the USS Maine a week later, pushed the U.S. toward war with Spain

events.title: Spanish American War
events.description: caused by election year and yellow journalism (exaggerated headlines) (Hearst and Pulitzer) on the sinking of USS Maine in Havana Harbor ('Remember the Maine')

events.title: Teller Amendment
events.description: gave Cuba freedom; declared that U.S. would not annex Cuba, but would leave its government to control the Cuban people after pacification

events.title: Williams v. Mississippi
events.description: upheld Mississippi's state constitution which allowed poll taxes, literacy tests, and grandfather clauses, essentially allowing disenfranchisement of African Americans

events.title: Hawaii obtained
events.description: U.S. officially annexes Hawaiian Islands

events.title: Peace of Paris
events.description: gave Cuba Independence, while U.S. gets Puerto Rico, Philippines, and Guam; major step in imperialism America

events.title: Anti-Imperialist League
events.description: opposed annexing the Philippines as a violation of self-government and the ideals of the Declaration of Independence; members included Mark Twain, Andrew Carnegie, and Jane Addams; some members also opposed annexation on racist grounds

events.title: Samoa divided
events.description: split between Germany and the United States, where western islands became German Samoa and eastern islands became American Samoa

events.title: Open Door Notes
events.description: open trade with China, suggesting no European country with holdings in China to stop trade with U.S.

events.title: Philippine-American War
events.description: Filipino nationalists led by Emilio Aguinaldo fought U.S. annexation; brutal guerrilla war killed over 4,000 U.S. soldiers and at least 200,000 Filipinos, mostly civilians who died from violence, disease, and famine; U.S. set up a colonial government under William Howard Taft

events.title: National Negro Business League
events.description: founded by Booker T. Washington to promote African American economic development; fostered Black-owned business and connected them to white business leaders; highlights intersection of race, business, and social reform

events.title: Gold Standard Act
events.description: gold as standard for nation's currency; effectively ended Silver Standard

events.title: Progressive Era
events.description: against corruption and monopolies, contributed temperance (self-control), helped immigrants and labor, safer building codes, and public utilities; characterized by industrialization, urbanization, and economic inequality

events.title: Boxer Rebellion
events.description: Chinese nationalist rebel against growing Japanese and Western influence in China, especially in trade and politics; international intervention from U.S., Britain, Russia, France, Germany, Japan, etc. to suppress rebellion

events.title: Roosevelt becomes president
events.description: McKinley, reelected in 1900 over Bryan (Dem), is assassinated; VP Theodore Roosevelt becomes president

events.title: U.S. Steel Corporation formed
events.description: combined Andrew Carnegie's Carnegie Steel Company with Gary's Federal Steel Company and Moore's National Steel Company; represented industrial growth and development

events.title: Platt Amendment
events.description: gave U.S. military base in Cuba and permission for troops to intervene and consent to treaties

events.title: Insular Cases
events.description: Constitution does not follow the flag; U.S. could rule Puerto Rico and other territories without Constitution

events.title: Big Stick Diplomacy
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt's foreign policy motto, 'speak softly and carry a big stick'; used the threat of military force, especially a strong navy, to protect U.S. interests in Latin America

events.title: Coal Strike
events.description: major labor union who struck for higher wages, shorter workdays, and recognition of union; U.S. intervened as a neutral arbitrator, marking turning point in relationship between government, business, and labor

events.title: Square Deal
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt's domestic policy platform; Three C's: Conservation of Natural Resources, Corporate Law, and Consumer Protection

events.title: Muckrakers
events.description: investigative journalists who exposed corruption and social problems: Ida Tarbell (Standard Oil), Lincoln Steffens (The Shame of the Cities, corrupt city governments), and Upton Sinclair (meatpacking); built public support for Progressive reforms

events.title: Department of Commerce and Labor
events.description: oversaw commerce and labor

events.title: Hay-Herran Treaty
events.description: wanted to buy land in Panama canal but was rejected by Colombia

events.title: Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty
events.description: Panamanians wanted Panama Canal as it would boost economy, so with U.S. naval support they revolted against Colombia; the new nation of Panama gave the U.S. land for the Canal Zone

events.title: Elkins Act
events.description: dealt with railroad rebates as part of Roosevelt's Square Deal

events.title: National Child Labor Committee
events.description: advocated for abolition of child labor; child labor played huge role as it was cheap and could be easily replaced, but caused a lot of harm to children

events.title: Northern Securities Co. v. U.S.
events.description: Supreme Court upheld Roosevelt's use of the Sherman Antitrust Act to break up J.P. Morgan's railroad holding company; Roosevelt became known as a 'trust buster' who distinguished between 'good' and 'bad' trusts

events.title: Roosevelt Corollary
events.description: addition to the Monroe Doctrine to make U.S. a police force, take over Dominican customs, and arbitrate Venezuela's dispute with Germany

events.title: Roosevelt elected
