events.description: Roosevelt wins a full term against Parker (Dem)

events.title: Industrial Workers of the World
events.description: radical labor union for all workers under one union for better working conditions, fair wages, and overthrow of the capitalist system; activism often clashed with government efforts for patriotism during World War I

events.title: Niagara Movement
events.description: W.E.B. Du Bois and other Black leaders demanded full civil and political rights, rejecting Booker T. Washington's gradual accommodation; led to the founding of the NAACP (1909)

events.title: The Jungle
events.description: written by Upton Sinclair, exposed the meat packing industry, resulting in the Meat Inspection Act as part of the Square Deal

events.title: Gentlemen's Agreement
events.description: with Japanese that Japanese could return to schools if Japan limits immigration

events.title: Treaty of Portsmouth
events.description: negotiated by T. Roosevelt for Russo-Japanese War; received a Nobel Peace Prize (1906) and further established U.S. as global intervention power

events.title: Hepburn Act
events.description: strengthened power of Interstate Commerce Commission

events.title: Pure Food and Drug Act
events.description: established Food and Drug Administration as a lot of processed food was not pure

events.title: Drago Doctrine
events.description: proposed by Argentine Foreign Minister that a country's failure to repay a national debt does not justify foreign intervention; suggested that Foreign, especially European powers should invest in Latin America at their own risk

events.title: Bank Panic
events.description: banks invested in stock exchange but stock exchange fell significantly and caused recession; many people had money either in stock or in banks that put their money in the stocks

events.title: Great White Fleet
events.description: Roosevelt sent 16 battleships on a world tour to display American naval power, especially to Japan

events.title: Muller v. Oregon
events.description: limited women work hours and dedicated that limiting the number of work hours for women did not violate the right to contract in the Fourteenth Amendment

events.title: Root-Takahira Agreement
events.description: Japan would honor Open Door Notes; furthered U.S. foreign power

events.title: Taft elected
events.description: defeats Bryan (Dem)

events.title: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP)
events.description: to combat discrimination of African Americans; included W.E.B. Du Bois and Mary White Ovington (women hoped suffrage and rights would eventually befall them)

events.title: Payne-Aldrich Tariff
events.description: promised to lower tariffs but made only small cuts and raised many rates; angered progressive Republicans who wanted lower tariffs and believed the act betrayed Republican principles

events.title: Ballinger-Pinchot Controversy
events.description: Gifford Pinchot, head of the Forest Service, accused Secretary of the Interior Richard Ballinger of opening protected public lands to private development; Taft fired Pinchot (1910); seen as betrayal of Roosevelt's conservation efforts, further splitting the Republican party

events.title: Dollar Diplomacy
events.description: Taft's foreign policy of using U.S. investment and loans rather than military force to extend influence in Latin America and East Asia; still led to military intervention, such as in Nicaragua (1912)

events.title: Standard Oil Company v. U.S.
events.description: ruled that the Standard Oil Co. violated the Sherman Antitrust Act and broke up monopoly; set precedent for future antitrust cases

events.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
events.description: fire in a New York garment factory killed 146 workers, mostly young immigrant women, because exits were locked; led to new workplace safety and labor laws

events.title: Wilson elected
events.description: Wilson beats T. Roosevelt (Progressive), Taft (Republican), and Debs (Socialist); Taft acts in Ballinger-Pinchot Controversy and Payne-Aldrich Tariff caused rift in Republicans that caused split of votes

events.title: moral diplomacy
events.description: foreign policy of Wilson that prioritized moral and ethical considerations in international relations, supporting countries with democratic governments while harming those with non-democratic regimes that were a threat to American ideals

events.title: New Nationalism vs. New Freedom
events.description: in the 1912 election, Theodore Roosevelt's New Nationalism accepted big business but called for strong federal regulation and social welfare programs, while Wilson's New Freedom sought to break up trusts and restore competition among small businesses

events.title: Sixteenth Amendment
events.description: authorized federal income tax, addressing economic inequality and providing the government with funds to social reforms

events.title: Seventeenth Amendment
events.description: direct popular election of Senate; gave more power to people and expanded voter participation; helped reduce influence of political machines and increased accountability of senators

events.title: Underwood Tariff
events.description: significantly lowered tariff rates and, under the new Sixteenth Amendment, created a graduated federal income tax to replace the lost revenue; part of Wilson's New Freedom

events.title: Federal Reserve Act
events.description: created a federal reserve system as the central bank of the U.S. to combat economic instability

events.title: Start of World War I
events.description: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia

events.title: Federal Trade Commission
events.description: independent federal agency tasked with protecting consumers and promoting competing

events.title: Clayton Antitrust Act
events.description: amendment to Sherman Anti-Trust Act; strengthened anti-monopolistic reform by targeting specific business practices that could lead to monopolies

events.title: U.S. invades Veracruz in Mexico
events.description: U.S. invades port of Veracruz in Mexico, Mexican forces detained nine American sailors; consequence of Wilson's moral diplomacy

events.title: Panama Canal opens
events.description: canal across Panama connected the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, greatly shortening shipping routes and boosting U.S. naval and commercial power; returned to Panama in 1999

events.title: Lusitania sunk
events.description: German U-boat sinks the British passenger liner Lusitania, killing nearly 1,200 people including 128 Americans; swayed public opinion against Germany, though the U.S. did not enter World War I until 1917

events.title: The Birth of a Nation
events.description: D.W. Griffith's film portrayed the Reconstruction-era Ku Klux Klan as heroes; protested by the NAACP; helped inspire the Klan's revival in 1915

events.title: Adamson Act
events.description: regulated the hours of workers in private companies, establishing eight-hour workday with overtime pay to railroad employees who worked on interstate commerce

events.title: Sussex Pledge
events.description: after a German U-boat attacked the French passenger ship Sussex, Germany promised not to sink merchant ships without warning; broken in 1917 when Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare

events.title: Punitive Expedition into Mexico
events.description: after Pancho Villa raided Columbus, New Mexico, Wilson sent General John J. Pershing into Mexico to capture him; Villa was never caught and U.S. troops withdrew in 1917

events.title: Wilson reelected
events.description: Wilson defeats Charles Evans Hughes (Rep) with the slogan 'He kept us out of war'

events.title: Zimmerman Note
events.description: message from German Foreign Secretary Zimmerman to German ambassador in Mexico; military alliance between Germany and Mexico if the U.S. entered World War I, where Germany would help Mexico regain lost land

events.title: U.S. enters World War I
events.description: Germany resumed submarine warfare and sent Zimmerman Note, effectively making U.S. an enemy

events.title: Selective Service Act
events.description: required men to register for the military draft; about 2.8 million men were drafted during World War I

events.title: War Industries Board
events.description: coordinated production and mobilization

events.title: Food Administration
events.description: headed by Hoover to ensure sufficient food supplies for both the American military and Allied forces; Lever Act set prices for agricultural products

events.title: Fuel Administration
events.description: headed by Harry Garfield to control fuel prices over concerns of fuel shortages for military and civilian needs

events.title: For/Against War
events.description: For: submarine warfare, destroying trade, violating rights, espionage and sabotage, Zimmerman Note, balance of power, save democracy; Against: only benefit wealthy, British violated our rights, Germany tried to avoid Lusitania, propaganda

events.title: First Red Scare
events.description: fear and paranoia regarding growth of communist or socialist ideologies, leading to mass arrests, deportations, and restricts of civil rights

events.title: Great Migration
events.description: blacks move from South to North in search of economic opportunity and to escape black discrimination in the South

events.title: Harlem Renaissance
events.description: cultural movement in Harlem, NYC, where African Americans celebrated identity and created new sense of pride through art, literature, and music (jazz); facilitated by Great Migration

events.title: Creel Committee
events.description: to promote support for World War I by influencing public opinion; used propaganda posters, films, and 'Four Minute Men' speakers, and promoted Liberty Bond drives

events.title: National War Labor Board
events.description: addressed labor disputes that could hinder war effort, effectively preventing strikes

events.title: Espionage and Sedition Acts
events.description: criminalized actions against war effort, government, flag, or military

events.title: Armistice Day
events.description: effective end of World War I on the Western Front; signed between Germany and Allies

events.title: Treaty of Versailles
events.description: officially ended World War I between Germany and the Allied Powers and required Germany to repay war debts

events.title: Wilson's Fourteen Points
events.description: vision for post-World War I peace; open covenants, disarmament, formation of Poland, freedom of seas and trade, rebuilding of Belgium, League of Nations (opposed by isolationist Republicans, etc.

events.title: Palmer Raids
events.description: suspending and deporting anarchists and communists as part of response to Red Scare

events.title: Schenck v. U.S.
events.description: 'clear and present danger'; open opposition to war will undermine war effort

events.title: Abrams v. U.S.
events.description: upheld Sedition Act

events.title: American Protective League
events.description: private pro-war volunteer group that worked with the Justice Department to spy on and harass Americans suspected of disloyalty, such as draft dodgers and German Americans; disbanded in 1919

events.title: Senate rejects Treaty of Versailles and League of Nations
events.description: Irreconcilables: believed it would infringe on American sovereignty, disagreement with Article X; Reservationists: accepted treaty if Article X would be clarified; only Congress can commit troops

events.title: Eighteenth Amendment
events.description: prohibited alcoholic beverages; people bootlegged or went to speakeasies (hidden bar that secretly sold alcoholic beverages

events.title: Race riots in Chicago/'Red Summer'
events.description: triggered by murder of Black teenager; increased racial tensions

events.title: Volstead Act
events.description: enforced Eighteenth Amendment by prohibiting production, sale, and transportation of alcohol

events.title: Nineteenth Amendment
events.description: women suffrage; huge success for women

events.title: Main Street
events.description: written by Sinclair Lewis, shows dissatisfaction of progressive women

events.title: First Commercial radio broadcast
events.description: brought in an era of connection with the country

events.title: Harding elected
events.description: beats Cox (Dem)

events.title: Roaring Twenties
events.description: economic prosperity with consumerism, explosion of art and entertainment, nativism and science vs. religion, and civil rights

events.title: American Birth Control League
events.description: women productive rights

events.title: Revenue Act
events.description: decreased taxes

events.title: Emergency Quota Act
events.description: limited yearly immigration from each country to 3% of the number of people from that country living in the U.S. in 1910; targeted Southern and Eastern European immigrants amid post-World War I nativism

events.title: Tulsa Race Massacre
events.description: white mob destroyed the prosperous Black Greenwood district ('Black Wall Street') in Tulsa, Oklahoma, killing an estimated 36 to 300 people; one of the worst incidents of racial violence in U.S. history

events.title: Washington Naval Conference
events.description: U.S., Britain, Japan, France, and Italy agreed to limit battleship tonnage (Five-Power Treaty, 5:5:3 ratio for the U.S., Britain, and Japan) and to respect each other's Pacific holdings; first major arms limitation agreement

events.title: Fordney-McCumber Tariff
events.description: raised tariffs to protect American industry and farmers; made it harder for Europeans to sell goods in the U.S. and repay their war debts

events.title: Teapot Dome Scandal
events.description: Secretary of the Interior Albert Fall secretly leased federal naval oil reserves at Teapot Dome, Wyoming, and Elk Hills, California, to private oil companies in exchange for bribes; Fall became the first Cabinet member sent to prison; symbol of corruption in the Harding administration

events.title: Coolidge becomes president
events.description: Harding dies suddenly while traveling; VP Calvin Coolidge becomes president

events.title: Dawes Plan
events.description: American loans to Germany helped it pay reparations to Britain and France, which then repaid their war debts to the U.S.; this circular flow of money collapsed with the Great Depression

events.title: Immigration Act of 1924 (National Origins Act)
events.description: cut quotas to 2% of each nationality based on the 1890 census, favoring Northern and Western Europeans over Southern and Eastern Europeans; barred immigration from Asia entirely

events.title: Indian Citizenship Act
events.description: granted U.S. citizenship to all Native Americans born in the U.S.

events.title: Coolidge elected to a full term
events.description: Coolidge defeats Davis (Dem) and La Follette (Progressive)

events.title: Scopes Trial
events.description: Tennessee teacher John Scopes was tried for teaching evolution in violation of the Butler Act; Clarence Darrow defended Scopes while William Jennings Bryan helped prosecute; Scopes was convicted (overturned on a technicality), but the trial exposed the clash between modernism and religious fundamentalism

events.title: Second Ku Klux Klan
events.description: revived Klan (refounded in 1915) grew to millions of members, including in the Midwest, and targeted Catholics, Jews, immigrants, and African Americans; declined after scandals in the late 1920s

events.title: Consumer culture and the automobile
events.description: mass production (Henry Ford's assembly line) made cars like the Model T affordable; advertising and installment buying (credit) spread consumer goods like radios and appliances; the automobile transformed suburbs, leisure, and the economy

events.title: Flappers
events.description: young women who challenged traditional norms with short hair, short skirts, and new social freedoms; symbolized changing gender roles, though most women's lives changed more slowly

events.title: Lost Generation
events.description: writers disillusioned by World War I and American materialism, such as F. Scott Fitzgerald (The Great Gatsby) and Ernest Hemingway

events.title: Marcus Garvey and the UNIA
events.description: Universal Negro Improvement Association promoted Black nationalism, racial pride, economic independence, and a 'Back to Africa' movement; Garvey was convicted of mail fraud and deported in 1927

events.title: Sacco and Vanzetti executed
events.description: Italian immigrant anarchists convicted of robbery and murder in 1921 in a trial marked by anti-immigrant and anti-radical prejudice; executed in 1927 despite worldwide protests

events.title: Kellogg-Briand Pact
events.description: agreement, eventually signed by over 60 nations, renouncing war as an instrument of national policy; had no means of enforcement

events.title: Hoover elected
events.description: Hoover (Rep) defeats Al Smith (Dem), the first Catholic major-party nominee; prosperity and anti-Catholic sentiment helped Hoover

events.title: Stock Market Crash ('Black Tuesday')
events.description: stock prices collapsed after years of speculation and buying stocks on margin (borrowed money); triggered the Great Depression

events.title: Great Depression
events.description: worst economic downturn in U.S. history; unemployment reached about 25% by 1933 and thousands of banks failed; caused by overproduction, unequal distribution of wealth, overuse of credit, a weak banking system, and the collapse of international trade; homeless people lived in shantytowns called 'Hoovervilles'

events.title: Hawley-Smoot Tariff
events.description: one of the highest tariffs in U.S. history; other countries retaliated with their own tariffs, worsening the collapse of world trade and the Depression

events.title: Reconstruction Finance Corporation
events.description: Hoover's program giving federal loans to banks, railroads, and large businesses, hoping benefits would 'trickle down'; criticized as too little and as favoring big business over direct relief for individuals

events.title: Bonus Army
events.description: thousands of World War I veterans marched on Washington demanding early payment of promised bonuses; Hoover had the army (led by Douglas MacArthur) forcibly clear their camp, damaging Hoover's reputation

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt elected
events.description: Roosevelt (Dem) defeats Hoover (Rep) in a landslide, promising a 'New Deal' for the American people

events.title: Twentieth Amendment
events.description: moved presidential inauguration from March 4 to January 20 and the start of congressional terms to January 3, shortening the 'lame duck' period

events.title: New Deal
events.description: Roosevelt's programs focused on the 'Three R's': relief for the unemployed, recovery of the economy, and reform of the financial system; greatly expanded the federal government's role in the economy and created the New Deal coalition of labor unions, urban immigrants, African Americans, farmers, and white Southerners

events.title: Emergency Banking Act
events.description: passed during the 'First Hundred Days'; after a national bank holiday, allowed sound banks to reopen under federal supervision; Roosevelt explained it in his first 'fireside chat' radio address, restoring public confidence

events.title: Glass-Steagall Act (FDIC)
events.description: separated commercial and investment banking and created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) to insure bank deposits

events.title: Civilian Conservation Corps
events.description: employed young men in conservation projects like planting trees, fighting soil erosion, and building parks

events.title: Agricultural Adjustment Act
events.description: paid farmers to reduce production in order to raise crop prices; struck down in U.S. v. Butler (1936) and revised in 1938; payments often went to landowners, who evicted tenant farmers and sharecroppers

events.title: Tennessee Valley Authority
events.description: federal corporation that built dams to provide cheap electricity, flood control, and jobs in the poor Tennessee River Valley

events.title: National Industrial Recovery Act
events.description: created the National Recovery Administration (NRA) to set industry codes for prices, wages, and hours, and guaranteed workers' right to organize; Public Works Administration built infrastructure; NRA struck down in Schechter Poultry Corp. v. U.S. (1935)

events.title: Good Neighbor Policy
events.description: Roosevelt pledged not to intervene militarily in Latin America; withdrew troops from Haiti and gave up the right to intervene in Cuba under the Platt Amendment (1934)

events.title: Twenty-first Amendment
events.description: repealed the Eighteenth Amendment, ending Prohibition

events.title: Indian Reorganization Act
events.description: 'Indian New Deal'; ended the Dawes Act's policy of dividing reservations into individual allotments and encouraged tribal self-government

events.title: Securities and Exchange Commission
events.description: regulated the stock market to prevent fraud and the reckless speculation that contributed to the 1929 crash

events.title: Critics of the New Deal
events.description: Huey Long ('Share Our Wealth'), Father Charles Coughlin (radio priest), and Dr. Francis Townsend (old-age pensions) argued the New Deal did not go far enough; the conservative American Liberty League argued it went too far and threatened free enterprise

events.title: Dust Bowl
events.description: severe drought and poor farming practices on the Great Plains caused massive dust storms; hundreds of thousands of 'Okies' migrated to California; depicted in John Steinbeck's The Grapes of Wrath (1939)

events.title: Works Progress Administration
events.description: largest New Deal jobs program, part of the 'Second New Deal'; employed millions to build roads, bridges, and schools, and also funded artists, writers, and musicians

events.title: Wagner Act (National Labor Relations Act)
events.description: guaranteed workers' right to form unions and bargain collectively, and created the National Labor Relations Board to enforce it; led to rapid union growth

events.title: Social Security Act
events.description: created old-age pensions, unemployment insurance, and aid to dependent children; initially excluded agricultural and domestic workers, leaving out many African Americans and women

events.title: Congress of Industrial Organizations (CIO)
events.description: led by John L. Lewis, organized unskilled workers by entire industry rather than by craft like the AFL; used sit-down strikes, such as at General Motors in Flint, Michigan (1936-1937), to win union recognition

events.title: Neutrality Acts
events.description: banned arms sales and loans to nations at war and barred Americans from traveling on ships of warring nations; reflected isolationism after the Nye Committee blamed bankers and arms makers for U.S. entry into World War I

events.title: Roosevelt reelected
events.description: Roosevelt defeats Landon (Rep) in a landslide, carrying every state except Maine and Vermont

events.title: Court-Packing Plan
events.description: after the Supreme Court struck down New Deal laws, Roosevelt proposed adding up to six new justices; rejected by Congress and criticized as an abuse of power, but the Court began upholding New Deal laws

events.title: Fair Labor Standards Act
events.description: set the first federal minimum wage (25 cents an hour) and a maximum workweek (later 40 hours), and restricted child labor; one of the last major New Deal reforms

events.title: World War II begins
events.description: Germany invades Poland; Britain and France declare war on Germany two days later

events.title: Neutrality Act of 1939 ('Cash and Carry')
events.description: allowed nations at war to buy American arms if they paid cash and carried them on their own ships; favored Britain and France, which controlled the seas

events.title: Destroyers-for-Bases Deal
events.description: U.S. gave Britain 50 old destroyers in exchange for leases on British naval bases in the Western Hemisphere

events.title: Selective Training and Service Act
events.description: first peacetime military draft in U.S. history

events.title: Roosevelt elected to a third term
events.description: Roosevelt defeats Willkie (Rep); broke the two-term tradition set by Washington

events.title: Four Freedoms speech
events.description: Roosevelt described four freedoms worth defending around the world: freedom of speech, freedom of worship, freedom from want, and freedom from fear

events.title: Lend-Lease Act
events.description: allowed the president to lend or lease weapons and supplies to nations whose defense was vital to the U.S.; made America the 'arsenal of democracy' for Britain and later the Soviet Union

events.title: Executive Order 8802
events.description: after A. Philip Randolph threatened a march on Washington, Roosevelt banned racial discrimination in defense industries and created the Fair Employment Practices Committee

events.title: Atlantic Charter
events.description: Roosevelt and Churchill outlined shared postwar goals: self-determination, free trade, no territorial expansion, and a new system of collective security (basis for the United Nations)

events.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.description: Japanese surprise attack on the U.S. naval base in Hawaii killed over 2,400 Americans; the U.S. declared war on Japan the next day, and Germany and Italy declared war on the U.S. on December 11

events.title: Japanese American internment
events.description: Executive Order 9066 led to the forced removal of about 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them U.S. citizens, from the West Coast to internment camps; upheld by the Supreme Court in Korematsu v. U.S. (1944)

events.title: Home front mobilization
events.description: War Production Board converted factories to war production, ending the Depression; rationing, war bonds, and price controls; women entered factory jobs ('Rosie the Riveter'); African Americans continued the Great Migration and pursued the 'Double V' campaign for victory against fascism abroad and racism at home

events.title: Bracero Program
events.description: agreement with Mexico bringing Mexican laborers to work on American farms and railroads during wartime labor shortages; lasted until 1964

events.title: Battle of Midway
events.description: turning point in the Pacific; the U.S. Navy sank four Japanese aircraft carriers, stopping Japanese expansion; followed by an 'island hopping' strategy toward Japan

events.title: Zoot Suit Riots
events.description: U.S. servicemen attacked Mexican American youths in Los Angeles; reflected wartime racial tensions

events.title: D-Day
events.description: Allied invasion of Normandy, France, commanded by Dwight D. Eisenhower; opened a second front in Western Europe against Germany

events.title: GI Bill (Servicemen's Readjustment Act)
events.description: gave veterans money for college and low-interest home and business loans; fueled postwar growth of the middle class and suburbs, though many Black veterans were denied benefits due to discrimination

events.title: Roosevelt elected to a fourth term
events.description: Roosevelt defeats Dewey (Rep), with Harry S. Truman as his new vice president

events.title: The Holocaust
events.description: Nazi Germany's systematic murder of about six million Jews and millions of others; the U.S. had restricted Jewish refugee immigration before the war; the full scale was revealed as Allied troops liberated the camps

events.title: Yalta Conference
events.description: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin agreed to divide Germany into occupation zones, hold free elections in Eastern Europe (which Stalin did not allow), have the Soviets enter the war against Japan, and create the United Nations

events.title: Truman becomes president
events.description: Roosevelt dies of a cerebral hemorrhage; VP Harry S. Truman becomes president

events.title: V-E Day
events.description: Germany surrenders unconditionally, ending the war in Europe

events.title: Potsdam Conference
events.description: Truman, Stalin, and Churchill (replaced mid-conference by Clement Attlee) discussed the occupation of Germany; the Potsdam Declaration demanded Japan's unconditional surrender; growing U.S.-Soviet tensions

events.title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
events.description: Truman ordered atomic bombs, developed by the secret Manhattan Project, dropped on Hiroshima (August 6) and Nagasaki (August 9), killing well over 100,000 people; justified as ending the war without a costly invasion of Japan; historians debate whether it was also meant to intimidate the Soviet Union

events.title: Japan surrenders
events.description: Japan announced its surrender on August 15 (V-J Day) and formally signed it aboard the USS Missouri on September 2, ending World War II

units.summary: U.S. rivalry with the Soviet Union and the expansion of communism, spread of youth culture, and civil rights movements

presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
presidents.description: Post World War II foreign policy and combatting spread of communism

presidents.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
presidents.description: Cold War policies

presidents.name: John F. Kennedy
presidents.description: New Frontier and Cold War crises; assassinated in office

presidents.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
presidents.description: Great Society, civil rights laws, and escalation of the Vietnam War

presidents.name: Richard Nixon
presidents.description: Vietnamization, détente, and the Watergate scandal; resigned

presidents.name: Gerald Ford
presidents.description: Pardoned Nixon and faced stagflation; only president never elected president or vice president

presidents.name: Jimmy Carter
presidents.description: Human rights diplomacy, Camp David Accords, energy crisis, and Iran hostage crisis

events.title: Cold War
events.description: rivalry between the U.S. (capitalism and democracy) and the Soviet Union (communism) that never became direct war between them; fought through the arms race, space race, proxy wars, alliances, and propaganda

events.title: United Nations founded
events.description: international organization to maintain peace; unlike the League of Nations, the U.S. joined and holds a permanent seat with veto power on the Security Council

events.title: Iron Curtain speech
events.description: Winston Churchill declared that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe, dividing Soviet-controlled Eastern Europe from the West

events.title: Containment
events.description: policy proposed by diplomat George Kennan to stop the spread of communism to new areas rather than roll it back; basis of U.S. Cold War foreign policy

events.title: Truman Doctrine
events.description: Truman pledged to support 'free peoples' resisting communist subjugation, beginning with $400 million in aid to Greece and Turkey

events.title: Taft-Hartley Act
events.description: passed over Truman's veto; limited union power by outlawing closed shops, allowing states to pass right-to-work laws, and letting the president impose an 80-day 'cooling off' period on strikes

events.title: National Security Act
events.description: reorganized the military under what became the Department of Defense and created the National Security Council and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)

events.title: Second Red Scare
events.description: fear of communist infiltration at home; loyalty reviews for federal employees; House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC) investigated Hollywood (Hollywood Ten); Alger Hiss convicted of perjury (1950); Julius and Ethel Rosenberg executed for atomic spying (1953)

events.title: Jackie Robinson breaks baseball's color line
events.description: joined the Brooklyn Dodgers as the first Black player in Major League Baseball in the modern era

events.title: Levittown
events.description: William Levitt's mass-produced suburban houses on Long Island symbolized the postwar suburban boom, aided by the GI Bill and federal (FHA) loans; excluded African American buyers

events.title: Marshall Plan
events.description: European Recovery Program gave about $13 billion to rebuild Western Europe, preventing the economic chaos that could lead to communism and creating markets for American goods; the Soviet bloc refused aid

events.title: Desegregation of the armed forces
events.description: Truman's Executive Order 9981 required equal treatment in the military, leading to its desegregation

events.title: Berlin Airlift
events.description: after the Soviets blockaded West Berlin, the U.S. and Britain flew in food and supplies for about a year until the Soviets lifted the blockade

events.title: Truman reelected
events.description: Truman (Dem) upsets Dewey (Rep) despite Democrats splitting into Dixiecrats (Strom Thurmond) and Progressives (Henry Wallace)

events.title: NATO formed
events.description: North Atlantic Treaty Organization; U.S. and Western European nations pledged that an attack on one was an attack on all; first U.S. peacetime military alliance outside the Western Hemisphere, breaking from the tradition of avoiding 'entangling alliances'

events.title: Soviet Union tests an atomic bomb
events.description: ended the U.S. nuclear monopoly and sped up the arms race; the U.S. responded by developing the hydrogen bomb (1952)

events.title: Communist Revolution in China
events.description: Mao Zedong's Communists defeated Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, who fled to Taiwan; Republicans blamed Truman for 'losing China'

events.title: NSC-68
events.description: secret National Security Council report calling for a massive military buildup to contain communism; put into effect after the Korean War began

events.title: McCarthyism
events.description: Senator Joseph McCarthy claimed to have a list of communists in the State Department and made reckless, unsupported accusations; discredited in the televised Army-McCarthy hearings (1954) and censured by the Senate

events.title: Korean War
events.description: North Korea invaded South Korea; UN forces led by the U.S. (General MacArthur) pushed toward the Chinese border until China intervened; Truman fired MacArthur (1951) for insubordination; the 1953 armistice left Korea divided near the 38th parallel

events.title: Twenty-second Amendment
events.description: limited presidents to two terms, in reaction to Roosevelt's four elections

events.title: Eisenhower elected
events.description: Eisenhower (Rep) defeats Stevenson (Dem), with Richard Nixon as vice president

events.title: Postwar affluence and suburbanization
events.description: baby boom (1946-1964); GI Bill and federal loans enabled suburban growth; spread of television, consumerism, and migration to the Sun Belt; emphasis on conformity and traditional gender roles, challenged by Beat writers and rock and roll youth culture

events.title: Warren Court
events.description: Chief Justice Earl Warren's Supreme Court expanded civil rights and civil liberties: Brown v. Board, Mapp v. Ohio (1961, illegally obtained evidence), Engel v. Vitale (1962, no official school prayer), Gideon, and Miranda

events.title: CIA covert operations
events.description: CIA helped overthrow the governments of Iran (1953) and Guatemala (1954), which the U.S. saw as threats to its interests

events.title: Brown v. Board of Education
events.description: Supreme Court overturned Plessy v. Ferguson's 'separate but equal' doctrine in public schools, ruling segregation inherently unequal; argued by NAACP lawyer Thurgood Marshall; desegregation proceeded slowly ('with all deliberate speed,' 1955)

events.title: 'New Look' and massive retaliation
events.description: Eisenhower and Secretary of State John Foster Dulles relied on nuclear weapons ('more bang for the buck') to deter Soviet aggression instead of costly conventional forces; brinkmanship

events.title: Domino theory
events.description: Eisenhower's belief that if one nation fell to communism, its neighbors would follow; justified U.S. involvement in Southeast Asia

events.title: Geneva Accords
events.description: after the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu, Vietnam was temporarily divided at the 17th parallel pending elections in 1956, which U.S.-backed South Vietnam refused to hold

events.title: Murder of Emmett Till
events.description: 14-year-old from Chicago murdered in Mississippi after being accused of offending a white woman; his mother's open-casket funeral drew national attention; his killers were acquitted by an all-white jury

events.title: Montgomery Bus Boycott
events.description: after Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat to a white passenger, Black residents boycotted Montgomery's buses for over a year under the leadership of Martin Luther King Jr.; ended when the Supreme Court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional

events.title: Southern Manifesto
events.description: 101 Southern members of Congress signed a statement opposing Brown v. Board; encouraged 'massive resistance' to desegregation

events.title: Federal-Aid Highway Act
events.description: funded the Interstate Highway System, justified partly for national defense; boosted suburbanization and car culture

events.title: Suez Crisis
events.description: U.S. pressured Britain, France, and Israel to withdraw after they invaded Egypt to seize the Suez Canal

events.title: Eisenhower reelected
events.description: Eisenhower defeats Stevenson (Dem) again

events.title: Eisenhower Doctrine
events.description: U.S. pledged economic and military aid to Middle Eastern nations resisting communism

events.title: Little Rock Nine
events.description: Arkansas governor Orval Faubus used the National Guard to block nine Black students from integrating Central High School; Eisenhower sent federal troops to enforce integration

events.title: Civil Rights Act of 1957
events.description: first civil rights law since Reconstruction; created the Civil Rights Commission and a Civil Rights Division in the Justice Department to protect voting rights; weakly enforced

events.title: Southern Christian Leadership Conference
events.description: civil rights organization led by Martin Luther King Jr.; used Black churches to organize nonviolent protest

events.title: Sputnik
events.description: Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite, sparking fears the U.S. was falling behind in science and missiles; led to the creation of NASA (1958) and the National Defense Education Act funding math and science education

events.title: Greensboro sit-ins
events.description: four Black college students sat at a segregated Woolworth's lunch counter in North Carolina; sit-ins spread across the South and led to the founding of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC)

events.title: U-2 Incident
events.description: Soviets shot down an American U-2 spy plane and captured pilot Francis Gary Powers; exposed Eisenhower's cover story and wrecked a planned summit

events.title: Eisenhower's Farewell Address
events.description: warned against the growing influence of the 'military-industrial complex'

events.title: Kennedy elected
events.description: Kennedy (Dem) narrowly defeats Nixon (Rep); first Catholic president; the first televised presidential debates helped Kennedy

events.title: New Frontier
events.description: Kennedy's domestic agenda of federal aid to education, health care for the elderly, and civil rights; most proposals stalled in Congress, but he expanded the space program (goal of landing on the Moon) and created the Peace Corps

events.title: Bay of Pigs Invasion
events.description: CIA-trained Cuban exiles failed to overthrow Fidel Castro; embarrassed Kennedy and pushed Cuba closer to the Soviet Union

events.title: Flexible response
events.description: Kennedy expanded conventional and special forces (Green Berets) so the U.S. could respond to conflicts without relying only on nuclear weapons

events.title: Freedom Rides
events.description: civil rights activists (CORE) rode interstate buses into the South to test rulings against segregated bus terminals; met by mob violence, which pressured the federal government to enforce desegregation

events.title: Berlin Wall built
events.description: East Germany built a wall to stop its people from fleeing to West Berlin; became the symbol of the Cold War

events.title: Silent Spring
events.description: Rachel Carson exposed the dangers of pesticides like DDT, sparking the modern environmental movement

events.title: Port Huron Statement
events.description: manifesto of Students for a Democratic Society (SDS) calling for 'participatory democracy'; beginning of the New Left student movement

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.description: U.S. discovered Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba; Kennedy ordered a naval 'quarantine'; after 13 days the Soviets removed the missiles in exchange for a U.S. pledge not to invade Cuba (and a secret removal of U.S. missiles from Turkey); closest the world came to nuclear war; led to a U.S.-Soviet hotline

events.title: The Feminine Mystique
events.description: Betty Friedan described the dissatisfaction of many suburban housewives ('the problem that has no name'); helped spark second-wave feminism

events.title: Gideon v. Wainwright
events.description: states must provide lawyers to criminal defendants who cannot afford one

events.title: Birmingham Campaign
events.description: King led protests against segregation in Birmingham, Alabama; police under Bull Connor used fire hoses and dogs on young marchers; King's 'Letter from Birmingham Jail' defended civil disobedience; televised images built support for civil rights legislation

events.title: Limited Test Ban Treaty
events.description: U.S., Britain, and the Soviet Union banned nuclear tests in the atmosphere, underwater, and in space

events.title: March on Washington
events.description: over 200,000 people marched for jobs and freedom; King delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech; built pressure for the Civil Rights Act

events.title: Lyndon B. Johnson becomes president
events.description: Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas, Texas by Lee Harvey Oswald; VP Lyndon B. Johnson is sworn in

events.title: Twenty-fourth Amendment
events.description: banned poll taxes in federal elections

events.title: Civil Rights Act of 1964
events.description: banned discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin in public accommodations and employment (Title VII); created the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission; passed after overcoming a Southern filibuster

events.title: Freedom Summer
events.description: volunteers registered Black voters in Mississippi; three civil rights workers (Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner) were murdered; the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party challenged the state's all-white delegation at the Democratic convention

events.title: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution
events.description: after reported attacks on U.S. destroyers off North Vietnam, Congress gave Johnson broad power to use military force in Vietnam without a declaration of war

events.title: Great Society
events.description: Johnson's domestic program to end poverty and racial injustice: the War on Poverty (Head Start, Job Corps), Medicare and Medicaid, federal aid to education, and civil rights laws; the largest expansion of the federal government since the New Deal

events.title: Johnson elected
events.description: Johnson (Dem) defeats Barry Goldwater (Rep) in a landslide; Goldwater's conservative campaign foreshadowed the rise of the New Right

events.title: Selma to Montgomery marches
events.description: on 'Bloody Sunday,' Alabama state troopers attacked voting rights marchers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge; televised violence built support for the Voting Rights Act

events.title: Escalation of the Vietnam War
events.description: Operation Rolling Thunder began sustained bombing of North Vietnam, and the first combat troops arrived; U.S. troop levels grew from about 184,000 at the end of 1965 to over 500,000 by 1968

events.title: Medicare and Medicaid
events.description: created federal health insurance for the elderly (Medicare) and the poor (Medicaid); part of the Great Society

events.title: Voting Rights Act of 1965
events.description: banned literacy tests and sent federal examiners to register voters in areas with a history of discrimination; dramatically increased Black voter registration in the South

events.title: Urban riots and the Kerner Commission
events.description: uprisings in Watts (Los Angeles, 1965), Newark, and Detroit (1967) over poverty and police brutality; the Kerner Commission (1968) blamed white racism and warned the nation was moving toward 'two societies, one black, one white—separate and unequal'

events.title: Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
events.description: ended the national origins quotas of the 1920s and prioritized family reunification and skills; led to large increases in immigration from Asia and Latin America

events.title: United Farm Workers
events.description: César Chávez and Dolores Huerta organized Mexican American and Filipino farmworkers; the Delano grape strike and national grape boycott (1965-1970) won union contracts

events.title: Antiwar movement
events.description: teach-ins, draft card burnings, and mass marches against the Vietnam War, led largely by college students; a 'credibility gap' grew between government claims and the reality of the war; divided Americans into 'hawks' and 'doves'

events.title: Miranda v. Arizona
events.description: police must inform suspects of their rights, including the right to remain silent and to have a lawyer, before questioning

events.title: National Organization for Women (NOW)
events.description: co-founded by Betty Friedan; pushed for equal pay, enforcement of the Civil Rights Act's ban on sex discrimination, and later the Equal Rights Amendment

events.title: Black Power movement
events.description: Stokely Carmichael (SNCC) and others rejected integration and strict nonviolence in favor of Black self-reliance and pride; influenced by Malcolm X (assassinated 1965); the Black Panther Party was founded in Oakland

events.title: Counterculture
events.description: young 'hippies' rejected mainstream values, embracing rock music, drug use, communal living, and the sexual revolution; peaked with the Woodstock festival (1969)

events.title: Tet Offensive
events.description: surprise attacks by North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces on South Vietnamese cities; a military defeat for the communists but it shattered public belief that the war was being won; Johnson announced he would not seek reelection

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. assassinated
events.description: killed in Memphis, Tennessee, sparking riots in over 100 cities; the Civil Rights Act of 1968 (Fair Housing Act) passed days later

events.title: Democratic National Convention in Chicago
events.description: after Robert F. Kennedy's assassination in June, police clashed violently with antiwar protesters outside the convention, deepening divisions in the Democratic Party

events.title: Nixon elected
events.description: Nixon (Rep) defeats Humphrey (Dem) and Wallace (American Independent); appealed to the 'silent majority' with a promise of 'law and order'; 'Southern strategy' drew white Southern voters toward the Republicans

events.title: Vietnamization
events.description: Nixon's policy of gradually withdrawing U.S. troops and turning the fighting over to South Vietnam, while expanding bombing; the Nixon Doctrine said allies must provide for their own defense

events.title: Stonewall Riots
events.description: a police raid on a gay bar in New York City led to days of protests; sparked the gay liberation movement

events.title: Moon landing
events.description: Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon, fulfilling Kennedy's goal and winning the space race

events.title: My Lai Massacre revealed
events.description: news broke that U.S. soldiers had killed hundreds of unarmed Vietnamese civilians in 1968; fueled antiwar sentiment

events.title: Invasion of Cambodia and Kent State shootings
events.description: Nixon expanded the war into Cambodia, sparking campus protests; National Guard troops killed four students at Kent State University in Ohio, and police killed two at Jackson State in Mississippi

events.title: Environmental Protection Agency
events.description: created by Nixon after the first Earth Day; followed by the Clean Air Act (1970), Clean Water Act (1972), and Endangered Species Act (1973)

events.title: Pentagon Papers
events.description: leaked by Daniel Ellsberg, a secret government history showing officials had misled the public about Vietnam; the Supreme Court allowed newspapers to publish them (New York Times v. U.S.)

events.title: Twenty-sixth Amendment
events.description: lowered the voting age to 18, since many young men drafted to fight in Vietnam could not vote

events.title: Nixon visits China
events.description: first U.S. president to visit the People's Republic of China; opened relations and took advantage of the split between China and the Soviet Union

events.title: Equal Rights Amendment passes Congress
events.description: proposed amendment guaranteeing equal rights regardless of sex; fell short of ratification after opposition led by conservative activist Phyllis Schlafly

events.title: Détente and SALT I
events.description: policy of easing tensions with the Soviet Union; the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (SALT I) and Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty limited nuclear weapons

events.title: Title IX
events.description: banned sex discrimination in federally funded education programs, greatly expanding women's athletics

events.title: Watergate scandal
events.description: burglars tied to Nixon's reelection committee broke into Democratic headquarters at the Watergate complex; Nixon's cover-up was exposed by reporters (Woodward and Bernstein), Senate hearings, and secret White House tapes

events.title: Nixon reelected
events.description: Nixon defeats McGovern (Dem) in a landslide

events.title: Paris Peace Accords
events.description: ended direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam and withdrew remaining American troops; fighting between North and South Vietnam continued

events.title: Roe v. Wade
events.description: Supreme Court ruled that the right to privacy protects a woman's decision to have an abortion, especially in early pregnancy; overturned in 2022 by Dobbs v. Jackson

events.title: American Indian Movement occupies Wounded Knee
events.description: activists occupied Wounded Knee, South Dakota, for 71 days to protest the federal government's treatment of Native Americans

events.title: OPEC oil embargo
events.description: Arab oil producers cut off oil to the U.S. for supporting Israel in the Yom Kippur War; gas shortages and soaring prices worsened 'stagflation'

events.title: War Powers Resolution
events.description: required the president to notify Congress within 48 hours of sending troops into combat and to withdraw them within 60 days (plus 30) without congressional approval; passed over Nixon's veto

events.title: United States v. Nixon
events.description: Supreme Court unanimously ruled that Nixon had to turn over the Watergate tapes; executive privilege is not absolute

events.title: Ford becomes president
events.description: Nixon resigns facing near-certain impeachment over Watergate, the only president to resign; Gerald Ford, appointed vice president after Spiro Agnew resigned in 1973, becomes president

events.title: Ford pardons Nixon
events.description: full pardon for any crimes Nixon may have committed as president; widely unpopular and hurt Ford's chances in 1976

events.title: Fall of Saigon
events.description: North Vietnam captured Saigon, unifying Vietnam under communist rule and ending the Vietnam War

events.title: Helsinki Accords
events.description: 35 nations, including the U.S. and Soviet Union, recognized post-World War II European borders and pledged to respect human rights

events.title: Stagflation
events.description: unusual combination of high inflation and high unemployment caused by oil shocks, foreign competition, and war spending; deindustrialization of the 'Rust Belt' and population shift to the Sun Belt

events.title: Carter elected
events.description: Carter (Dem), a Washington outsider promising honesty after Watergate, defeats Ford (Rep)

events.title: Panama Canal Treaties
events.description: agreed to transfer control of the Panama Canal to Panama by the end of 1999

events.title: Camp David Accords
events.description: Carter brokered peace between Egypt (Anwar Sadat) and Israel (Menachem Begin); Egypt recognized Israel and Israel returned the Sinai Peninsula

events.title: Regents of the University of California v. Bakke
events.description: Supreme Court ruled racial quotas in admissions unconstitutional but allowed race to be considered as one factor in affirmative action

events.title: Proposition 13
events.description: California voters sharply limited property taxes, sparking a national 'tax revolt' that helped the conservative movement

events.title: Three Mile Island
events.description: partial meltdown at a nuclear power plant in Pennsylvania increased public opposition to nuclear power

events.title: Energy crisis
events.description: the Iranian Revolution cut oil supplies, causing a second oil shock and gas lines; Carter had created the Department of Energy (1977), urged conservation, and gave his 'Crisis of Confidence' ('malaise') speech

events.title: Moral Majority
events.description: founded by Reverend Jerry Falwell to mobilize evangelical Christians in politics; part of the rising New Right

events.title: Iran Hostage Crisis
events.description: after the Iranian Revolution overthrew the U.S.-backed Shah, militants seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran and held 52 Americans hostage for 444 days; a failed rescue mission (1980) hurt Carter; the hostages were released minutes after Reagan's inauguration

events.title: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
events.description: ended détente; Carter withdrew the SALT II treaty from Senate consideration, boycotted the 1980 Moscow Olympics, and announced the Carter Doctrine to defend the Persian Gulf; the U.S. armed the Afghan resistance (mujahideen)

units.summary: Advance of political conservatism, developments in science and technology, demographic shifts, and the early 21st century

presidents.name: Ronald Reagan
presidents.description: Conservative revival, Reaganomics, and the late Cold War

presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
presidents.description: End of the Cold War and the Persian Gulf War

presidents.name: Bill Clinton
presidents.description: Centrist 'New Democrat'; economic boom, NAFTA, and impeachment

presidents.name: George W. Bush
presidents.description: September 11 attacks, the War on Terror, and the Great Recession

presidents.name: Barack Obama
presidents.description: First African American president; Great Recession recovery and the Affordable Care Act

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.description: 'America First' trade and immigration policies; impeached twice and acquitted both times

presidents.name: Joe Biden
presidents.description: COVID-19 recovery, infrastructure and climate spending, and support for Ukraine

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.description: Second president to serve non-consecutive terms

events.title: Reagan elected
events.description: Reagan (Rep) defeats Carter (Dem) and Anderson (Independent) amid high inflation and the Iran hostage crisis

events.title: Rise of the New Right
events.description: conservative coalition of evangelical Christians (Moral Majority), fiscal conservatives, and anti-communists; opposed big government, high taxes, abortion, and the Equal Rights Amendment; carried Reagan to victory ('Reagan Revolution')

events.title: Reaganomics
events.description: supply-side ('trickle-down') economics: large tax cuts (Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981), deregulation, and cuts to domestic programs, while greatly increasing military spending; inflation fell, but federal deficits and the national debt soared

events.title: PATCO strike
events.description: Reagan fired over 11,000 striking air traffic controllers, weakening the labor movement

events.title: Sandra Day O'Connor appointed
events.description: first woman on the Supreme Court

events.title: AIDS epidemic
events.description: first cases reported in 1981; the disease was stigmatized and at first largely ignored by the government; activists such as ACT UP pushed for research and treatment

events.title: Reagan Doctrine
events.description: Reagan called the Soviet Union an 'evil empire' and supported anti-communist forces around the world, such as the Contras in Nicaragua and the mujahideen in Afghanistan; invaded Grenada (1983)

events.title: Strategic Defense Initiative
events.description: proposed space-based missile defense system nicknamed 'Star Wars'; part of a massive defense buildup that strained the Soviet economy as it tried to keep up

events.title: Beirut barracks bombing
events.description: suicide truck bombing killed 241 U.S. servicemen on a peacekeeping mission in Lebanon; U.S. troops withdrew soon after

events.title: Reagan reelected
events.description: Reagan defeats Mondale (Dem), whose running mate Geraldine Ferraro was the first woman on a major-party ticket; Reagan won 49 states

events.title: Gorbachev's reforms
events.description: Mikhail Gorbachev became Soviet leader and introduced glasnost (openness) and perestroika (economic restructuring), easing Cold War tensions

events.title: Iran-Contra Affair
events.description: Reagan administration officials secretly sold weapons to Iran and illegally used the profits to fund the Contra rebels in Nicaragua, despite a congressional ban (Boland Amendment)

events.title: Immigration Reform and Control Act
events.description: granted legal status to nearly 3 million undocumented immigrants who had arrived before 1982, while penalizing employers who knowingly hired undocumented workers

events.title: INF Treaty
events.description: Reagan and Gorbachev agreed to eliminate intermediate-range nuclear missiles, the first treaty to reduce rather than just limit nuclear arsenals; same year as Reagan's 'Tear down this wall!' speech in Berlin

events.title: George H. W. Bush elected
events.description: Bush (Rep), Reagan's vice president, defeats Dukakis (Dem); promised 'Read my lips: no new taxes'

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: East Germany opened its border; peaceful revolutions overthrew communist governments across Eastern Europe, and Germany reunified in 1990

events.title: Americans with Disabilities Act
events.description: banned discrimination against people with disabilities in employment and public places and required accessibility

events.title: Bush breaks 'no new taxes' pledge
events.description: agreed to a budget deal with tax increases to reduce the deficit; angered conservatives and hurt his reelection chances

events.title: Persian Gulf War
events.description: after Iraq (Saddam Hussein) invaded Kuwait, a U.S.-led UN coalition drove Iraqi forces out in Operation Desert Storm; quick victory; Bush proclaimed a 'new world order'

events.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.description: Soviet Union broke apart into 15 independent republics, ending the Cold War and leaving the U.S. as the world's only superpower

events.title: Los Angeles riots
events.description: riots broke out after police officers were acquitted in the videotaped beating of Rodney King; highlighted racial tensions and police brutality

events.title: Clinton elected
events.description: Clinton (Dem) defeats Bush (Rep) and Ross Perot (Independent), who won about 19% of the popular vote; campaigned as a centrist 'New Democrat' focused on the economy

events.title: Globalization and the digital revolution
events.description: growth of personal computers and the internet fueled a tech ('dot-com') boom and economic growth; globalization increased trade, outsourcing of manufacturing, and immigration

events.title: 'Don't Ask, Don't Tell'
events.description: compromise policy allowing gay and lesbian Americans to serve in the military only if they kept their sexual orientation secret; ended in 2011

events.title: Failed health care reform
events.description: Clinton's plan for universal health coverage, led by First Lady Hillary Clinton, was defeated in Congress

events.title: NAFTA takes effect
events.description: North American Free Trade Agreement, negotiated under Bush and passed under Clinton, removed most trade barriers between the U.S., Canada, and Mexico; increased trade but was criticized for moving manufacturing jobs abroad

events.title: Contract with America
events.description: Republicans led by Newt Gingrich promised smaller government, tax cuts, and welfare reform, winning control of both houses of Congress for the first time in 40 years

events.title: Oklahoma City bombing
events.description: domestic terrorist Timothy McVeigh bombed a federal building, killing 168 people

events.title: Welfare reform
events.description: Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act replaced Aid to Families with Dependent Children with Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), adding work requirements and time limits

events.title: Defense of Marriage Act
events.description: defined marriage for federal purposes as between a man and a woman; key part struck down in U.S. v. Windsor (2013)

events.title: Clinton reelected
events.description: Clinton defeats Dole (Rep) and Perot (Reform)

events.title: Federal budget surplus
events.description: first balanced budget with a surplus since 1969, thanks to the economic boom, tax increases, and spending cuts

events.title: Clinton impeached
events.description: House impeached Clinton for perjury and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky scandal; the Senate acquitted him

events.title: George W. Bush elected
events.description: Bush (Rep) defeats Gore (Dem) despite losing the popular vote; the Supreme Court stopped the Florida recount in Bush v. Gore

events.title: September 11 attacks
events.description: al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four planes, destroying the World Trade Center and damaging the Pentagon; nearly 3,000 people were killed; launched the 'War on Terror'

events.title: USA PATRIOT Act
events.description: expanded government surveillance powers to fight terrorism; sparked debate over civil liberties

events.title: War in Afghanistan
events.description: U.S. invaded to overthrow the Taliban government, which sheltered al-Qaeda; longest war in U.S. history; U.S. withdrew in 2021 and the Taliban returned to power

events.title: No Child Left Behind Act
events.description: increased the federal role in education through standardized testing and school accountability

events.title: Department of Homeland Security
events.description: created to coordinate counterterrorism and domestic security agencies

events.title: Iraq War
events.description: under the Bush Doctrine of preemptive war, the U.S. invaded Iraq citing weapons of mass destruction (none were found) and ties to terrorism; overthrew Saddam Hussein, but a long insurgency followed; U.S. troops left in 2011

events.title: Demographic shifts
events.description: Latinos became the largest minority group by the early 2000s, and the Asian American population grew through immigration; population and political power shifted to the Sun Belt; debates over immigration reform and an aging Baby Boom generation

events.title: Bush reelected
events.description: Bush defeats Kerry (Dem)

events.title: Hurricane Katrina
events.description: devastated New Orleans and the Gulf Coast; the slow federal response was criticized, especially for its impact on poor and Black residents

events.title: Great Recession
events.description: housing bubble burst and risky subprime mortgages caused major bank failures; the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP, 2008) bailed out banks; worst economic downturn since the Great Depression

events.title: Obama elected
events.description: Barack Obama (Dem) defeats McCain (Rep), becoming the first African American president

events.title: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act
events.description: stimulus package of about $800 billion in spending and tax cuts to fight the Great Recession

events.title: Tea Party movement
events.description: conservative movement opposing government spending, taxes, and the Affordable Care Act; helped Republicans win the House in 2010

events.title: Affordable Care Act ('Obamacare')
events.description: expanded health insurance through marketplaces and Medicaid expansion, and protected people with preexisting conditions; required most Americans to have insurance (upheld in NFIB v. Sebelius, 2012)

events.title: Dodd-Frank Act
events.description: increased regulation of the financial industry after the Great Recession and created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

events.title: Citizens United v. FEC
events.description: Supreme Court ruled that corporations and unions can spend unlimited amounts on independent political advertising as free speech

events.title: Osama bin Laden killed
events.description: U.S. Navy SEALs killed the al-Qaeda leader in a raid in Pakistan

events.title: DACA
events.description: Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals protected undocumented immigrants brought to the U.S. as children from deportation

events.title: Obama reelected
events.description: Obama defeats Romney (Rep)

events.title: Shelby County v. Holder
events.description: Supreme Court struck down the Voting Rights Act formula that determined which states needed federal approval before changing voting laws

events.title: Black Lives Matter
events.description: movement against police violence and systemic racism; grew after police killings of Black Americans such as Michael Brown (2014) and George Floyd (2020), which sparked nationwide protests

events.title: Obergefell v. Hodges
events.description: Supreme Court ruled that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry nationwide

events.title: Paris Climate Agreement
events.description: international agreement to reduce greenhouse gas emissions; the U.S. later withdrew, rejoined, and withdrew again as administrations changed

events.title: Trump elected
events.description: Donald Trump (Rep) defeats Hillary Clinton (Dem), the first woman nominated by a major party, despite losing the popular vote

events.title: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
events.description: cut the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21% and lowered individual income tax rates

events.title: Trade war and USMCA
events.description: Trump placed tariffs on imports such as steel, aluminum, and many Chinese goods as part of 'America First' policy; NAFTA was replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA, in effect 2020)

events.title: Trump impeached twice
events.description: impeached by the House in 2019 for abuse of power and obstruction of Congress (related to Ukraine) and in 2021 for incitement of insurrection after the January 6 attack on the Capitol; acquitted by the Senate both times

events.title: COVID-19 pandemic
events.description: global pandemic that killed over one million Americans; lockdowns caused a sharp recession; the CARES Act provided economic relief, and vaccines were developed rapidly (Operation Warp Speed)

events.title: Biden elected
events.description: Joe Biden (Dem) defeats Trump (Rep); Kamala Harris became the first woman vice president; Trump's claims of widespread fraud were rejected by the courts, and his supporters stormed the Capitol on January 6, 2021 to stop certification of the results

events.title: American Rescue Plan
events.description: $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief package

events.title: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
events.description: bipartisan law providing about $1.2 trillion for roads, bridges, broadband internet, and public transit

events.title: Russia invades Ukraine
events.description: the U.S. and NATO allies sent billions of dollars in military and economic aid to Ukraine and placed sanctions on Russia

events.title: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
events.description: Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, returning the regulation of abortion to the states

events.title: Inflation Reduction Act
events.description: invested in clean energy and climate programs and allowed Medicare to negotiate the prices of some prescription drugs

events.title: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
events.description: Supreme Court ended race-conscious affirmative action in college admissions

events.title: Trump elected
events.description: Trump (Rep) defeats Kamala Harris (Dem), who replaced Biden as the Democratic nominee; second president after Grover Cleveland elected to non-consecutive terms
